Let these be $h,h-1.$ Let their parents be $\mathsf{par}(h-1)$ and $\mathsf{par}(h).$ We rewrite Proposition 1.3 in a way that allows us to compare to signed 2-stars and 4-cycles. Applying the leaf-isolation technique in Eq. 14

$$ \displaystyle\Bigg|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(H)\Bigg| \displaystyle\leq\sum_{x_{1},x_{2},\ldots,x_{h-2}}\Bigg(p_{x_{1}}p_{x_{2}}\cdots p_{x_{h-2}}\prod_{(ij)\in\mathsf{E}(H)\backslash\{(\mathsf{par}(h-1),h-1),(\mathsf{par}(h),h)\}}|Q_{x_{i},x_{j}}|\times \displaystyle\quad\quad\quad\quad\times\bigg(\big(\sum_{x_{h-1}}p_{x_{h-1}}Q_{x_{\mathsf{par}(h-1)},x_{h-1}}\big)^{2}+\big(\sum_{x_{h}}p_{x_{h}}Q_{x_{\mathsf{par}(h)},x_{h}}\big)^{2}\bigg)\Bigg) $$

We used the simple inequality $|a|\times|b|\leq a^{2}+b^{2}.$ We now interpret the terms above.

#### Square Terms and 2-Stars.

From Corollary 2.2 and the fact that $p_{i}\geq c>0$ for any $i,$

$$ \displaystyle\big(\sum_{x_{h-1}}p_{x_{h-1}}Q_{x_{\mathsf{par}(h-1)},x_{h-1}}\big)^{2}+\big(\sum_{x_{h}}p_{x_{h}}Q_{x_{\mathsf{par}(h)}x_{h}}\big)^{2} \displaystyle\lesssim_{c}p_{\mathsf{par}(h-1)}\big(\sum_{x_{h-1}}p_{x_{h-1}}Q_{x_{\mathsf{par}(h-1)},x_{h-1}}\big)^{2}+p_{\mathsf{par}(h)}\big(\sum_{x_{h}}p_{x_{h}}Q_{x_{\mathsf{par}(h)}x_{h}}\big)^{2} \displaystyle\lesssim_{c}\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{2}). $$

#### 4-Cycles.

Now, by Lemma 3.2,

$$ \displaystyle\sum_{x_{1},x_{2},\ldots,x_{h-2}}p_{x_{1}}p_{x_{2}}\cdots p_{x_{h-2}}\prod_{(ij)\in\mathsf{E}(H)\backslash\{(\mathsf{par}(h-1),h-1),(\mathsf{par}(h),h)\}}|Q_{x_{i},x_{j}}| \displaystyle\leq\sum_{x_{1},x_{2},\ldots,x_{h-2}}p_{x_{1}}p_{x_{2}}\ldots p_{x_{h-2}}(\max_{u,v}|Q_{u,v}|)^{|\mathsf{E}(H)|-2} \displaystyle=(\max_{u,v}|Q_{u,v}|)^{|\mathsf{V}(H)|-3} \displaystyle\lesssim_{c,D}|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4})|^{\frac{|\mathsf{V}(H)|-3}{4}}. $$

Altogether, we obtain that

$$ \begin{split}&\big|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(H)\big|\lesssim_{c,D}\big|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{2})\big|\times|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4})|^{\frac{|\mathsf{V}(H)|-3}{4}}.\end{split} $$

We now proceed similarly to Corollary 2.1. Namely, we rewrite

$$ \begin{split}&\big|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(H)\big|^{\frac{1}{|\mathsf{V}(H)|}}\lesssim_{c,D}\big|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{2})\big|^{\frac{1}{|\mathsf{V}(H)|}}\times|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4})|^{\frac{|\mathsf{V}(H)|-3}{4}\times\frac{1}{|\mathsf{V}(H)|}}\Longleftrightarrow\\
&\big|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(H)\big|^{\frac{1}{|\mathsf{V}(H)|}}\lesssim_{c,D}\Bigg(\big|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{2})\big|^{\frac{1}{3}}\Bigg)^{\frac{3}{|\mathsf{V}(H)|}}\times\Bigg(\big|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4})\big|^{\frac{1}{4}}\Bigg)^{\frac{|\mathsf{V}(H)|-3}{|\mathsf{V}(H)|}}\end{split} $$

As $\frac{|\mathsf{V}(H)|-3}{|\mathsf{V}(H)|}+\frac{3}{|\mathsf{V}(H)|}=1,$ the conclusion follows. ∎ Again, Theorem 2.4 applied for any $D\geq 8$ gives the corresponding testing result.

#### Theorem 3.5 (Testing in Non-Vanishing Community Probabilities).

Suppose that $c>0$ is an absolute constant and $\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)$ is an SBM model on $k$ communities such that $p_{i}>c\quad\forall i\in[k].$ If there exists a constant degree test distinguishing ${\mathbb{G}(n,1/2)}$ and $\mathbb{SBM}(n;p,Q)$ with high probability, one can also distinguish the two distributions with high probability using the signed count of one of the $\mathsf{Star}_{1}$ (edge), $\mathsf{Star}_{2}$ (wedge), or $\mathsf{Cyc}_{4}$ (4-cycle) graphs.

### 3.4 General 2-SBMs

#### Theorem 3.6 (Maximizing Partition Functions in 2-SBMs).

Let $D\in\mathbb{N}$ be some fixed even natural number. Suppose that $\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)$ is an arbitrary SBM on $k=2$ communities. Then, for any connected graph $H$ on at most $D$ edges,

$$ \Psi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(H)\lesssim_{D}\max\Bigg(\Psi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4}),\max_{1\leq t\leq D}\Psi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{t})\Bigg). $$

Due to the length and complexity of the proof, we split it into several sections. Without loss of generality suppose that $p_{1}\leq p_{2}.$ As $p_{1}+p_{2}=1,$ this means that $p_{2}\geq 1/2.$

We will also use throughout the following simple claim about signed 4-cycles in 2-SBMs.

#### Claim 3.4.

Whenever $p_{2}\geq p_{1}$ in a 2-community stochastic block model $\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q),$

$$ \Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4})=\Theta(\max(p_{1}^{4}Q_{1,1}^{4},p_{1}^{2}Q_{1,2}^{4},Q_{2,2}^{4})). $$

#### Proof.

Expanding Proposition 1.3,

$$ \displaystyle\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4})=p_{1}^{4}Q_{1,1}^{4}+4p_{1}^{3}p_{2}Q_{1,1}^{2}Q_{1,2}^{2}+4p_{1}^{2}p_{2}^{2}Q_{1,1}Q_{1,2}^{2}Q_{2,2} \displaystyle\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad+2p_{1}^{2}p_{2}^{2}Q_{1,2}^{4}+4p_{1}p_{2}^{3}Q_{1,2}^{2}Q_{2,2}^{2}+p_{2}^{4}Q_{2,2}^{4}. $$

Observe that $|4p_{1}^{2}p_{2}^{2}Q_{1,1}Q_{1,2}^{2}Q_{2,2}|\leq 2p_{1}^{3}p_{2}Q_{1,1}^{2}Q_{1,2}^{2}+2p_{1}p_{2}^{3}Q_{1,2}^{2}Q_{2,2}^{2}$ by AM-GM. Hence the above expression is bounded between $p_{1}^{4}Q_{1,1}^{4}+2p_{1}^{3}p_{2}Q_{1,1}^{2}Q_{1,2}^{2}+2p_{1}^{2}p_{2}^{2}Q_{1,2}^{4}+2p_{1}p_{2}^{3}Q_{1,2}^{2}Q_{2,2}^{2}+p_{2}^{4}Q_{2,2}^{4}$ and $p_{1}^{4}Q_{1,1}^{4}+6p_{1}^{3}p_{2}Q_{1,1}^{2}Q_{1,2}^{2}+2p_{1}^{2}p_{2}^{2}Q_{1,2}^{4}+6p_{1}p_{2}^{3}Q_{1,2}^{2}Q_{2,2}^{2}+p_{2}^{4}Q_{2,2}^{4}.$ Similarly, observe that $0\leq 2p_{1}^{3}p_{2}Q_{1,1}^{2}Q_{1,2}^{2}\leq p_{1}^{4}Q_{1,1}^{4}+p_{1}^{2}p_{2}^{2}Q_{1,2}^{2}.$ Using also that $p_{2}\in[1/2,1)$ gives the desired conclusion. ∎

$$ \begin{split}&|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(H)|^{\frac{1}{|\mathsf{V}(H)|}}=\Bigg|\sum_{x_{1},x_{2},\ldots,x_{h}\in[k]}\Bigg(\prod_{i=1}^{h}p_{x_{i}}\times\prod_{(i,j)\in\mathsf{E}(H)}Q_{x_{i},x_{j}}\Bigg)\Bigg|^{\frac{1}{|\mathsf{V}(H)|}}\\

#### 3.4.3 Step 3: Within-community Cancellations.

We begin by analyzing the case of within-community cancellations which turns out to be the simpler case.

#### Lemma 3.5.

Suppose that (30) and (31) hold for some $C\geq 4.$ Then, $|Q_{1,2}|\leq Cp_{1}|Q_{1,1}|.$

#### Proof.

Case 1) First, suppose that (31.a) holds. Then,

$$ (p_{1}|Q_{1,1}|+p_{2}|Q_{1,2}|)\geq C\Big|p_{1}Q_{1,1}+p_{2}Q_{1,2}\Big|\geq C\Big|p_{1}|Q_{1,1}|-p_{2}|Q_{1,2}|\Big|. $$

When $C\geq 4,$ this immediately implies that $p_{2}|Q_{1,2}|\leq 2p_{1}|Q_{1,1}|$ which is enough as $p_{2}\geq 1/2.$

Case 2) Now, suppose that that (31.b) holds. Then, $p_{1}|Q_{1,2}|+p_{2}|Q_{2,2}|\geq C\Big|p_{1}Q_{1,2}+p_{2}Q_{2,2}\Big|\geq C\Big|p_{1}|Q_{1,2}|-p_{2}|Q_{2,2}|\Big|.$ As in Case 1), $p_{2}|Q_{2,2}|\leq 2p_{1}|Q_{1,2}|.$ Hence, $(p_{1}|Q_{1,2}|+p_{2}|Q_{2,2}|)\leq 3p_{1}|Q_{1,2}|,$ so

$$ \displaystyle\Big|p_{1}Q_{1,2}+p_{2}Q_{2,2}\Big|\leq\frac{1}{C}(p_{1}|Q_{1,2}|+p_{2}|Q_{2,2}|)\leq\frac{3}{C}p_{1}|Q_{1,2}| $$

There are two cases. Either $|p_{1}Q_{1,1}+p_{2}Q_{1,2}|\leq\frac{1}{\sqrt{C}}(p_{1}|Q_{1,1}|+p_{2}|Q_{1,2}|),$ which immediately implies $p_{2}|Q_{1,2}|\leq 2p_{1}|Q_{1,1}|$ as in Case 1) provided $C\geq 4^{2}.$ Or,

$$ \begin{split}&|p_{1}Q_{1,1}+p_{2}Q_{1,2}|>\frac{1}{\sqrt{C}}(p_{1}|Q_{1,1}|+p_{2}|Q_{1,2}|)\geq\frac{1}{\sqrt{C}}p_{2}|Q_{1,2}|\geq\frac{1}{2\sqrt{C}}|Q_{1,2}|.\end{split} $$

Combining (33) and (34),

$$ \displaystyle\Bigg|p_{1}(p_{1}Q_{1,1}+p_{2}Q_{1,2})^{\mathbf{T}}+p_{2}(pQ_{1,2}+p_{2}Q_{2,2})^{\mathbf{T}}\Bigg| \displaystyle\geq\Bigg|p_{1}(p_{1}Q_{1,1}+p_{2}Q_{1,2})^{\mathbf{T}}\Bigg|-\Bigg|p_{2}(pQ_{1,2}+p_{2}Q_{2,2})^{\mathbf{T}}\Bigg| \displaystyle\geq p_{1}\times\Big(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{C}}|Q_{1,2}|\Big)^{\mathbf{T}}-p_{2}\Big(\frac{3}{C}p_{1}|Q_{1,2}|\Big)^{\mathbf{T}} \displaystyle\geq p_{1}\times\Big(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{C}}|Q_{1,2}|\Big)^{\mathbf{T}}-p_{1}\Big(\frac{3}{C}|Q_{1,2}|\Big)^{\mathbf{T}} \displaystyle\geq\frac{p_{1}|Q_{1,2}|^{\mathbf{T}}}{(2C)^{\mathbf{T}}} $$

whenever $C\geq 128.$

Now, recall (30). Then, as $(p_{1}|Q_{1,2}|+p_{2}|Q_{2,2}|)\leq 3p_{1}|Q_{1,2}|,$ it must be the case that

$$ \displaystyle p_{1}(p_{1}|Q_{1,1}|+p_{2}|Q_{1,2}|)^{\mathbf{T}}+p_{2}(3p_{1}|Q_{1,2}|)^{\mathbf{T}} \displaystyle\geq p_{1}(p_{1}|Q_{1,1}|+p_{2}|Q_{1,2}|)^{\mathbf{T}}+p_{2}(p_{1}|Q_{1,2}|+p_{2}|Q_{2,2}|)^{\mathbf{T}} \displaystyle\geq(4C^{2})^{\mathbf{T}}\Bigg|p_{1}(p_{1}Q_{1,1}+p_{2}Q_{1,2})^{\mathbf{T}}+p_{2}(p_{1}Q_{1,2}+p_{2}Q_{2,2})^{\mathbf{T}}\Bigg| \displaystyle\geq(4C^{2})^{\mathbf{T}}\frac{p_{1}|Q_{1,2}|^{\mathbf{T}}}{(2C)^{\mathbf{T}}}. $$

For large enough $C\geq 128,$ this immediately implies that

$$ p_{1}|Q_{1,1}|+p_{2}|Q_{1,2}|\geq\frac{3C}{2}\times|Q_{1,2}|. $$

Again, this implies $|Q_{1,2}|\leq Cp_{1}|Q_{1,1}|.$ ∎

It turns out that Lemma 3.5 is enough to imply Theorem 3.6.

#### Lemma 3.6.

Suppose that $|Q_{1,2}|\leq Cp_{1}|Q_{1,1}|$ for some absolute constant $C.$ Then, for any connected graph $H$ on at most $D$ edges,

$$ \begin{split}&\Psi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(H)\lesssim_{D}\max\Bigg(\Psi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4}),\max_{1\leq t\leq D}\Psi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{t})\Bigg).\end{split} $$

In the rest of the section, we prove Lemma 3.6. Again, the proof depends on whether $H$ is a tree.

#### Proof of Lemma 3.6 when $H$ is not a tree.

Suppose that $H$ is connected and not a tree. Then, $H$ has at least $|\mathsf{V}(H)|$ edges. Now, we rewrite Proposition 1.3 as follows:

$$ \begin{split}&\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(H)\\
&=\sum_{x_{1},x_{2},\ldots,x_{h}\in\{1,2\}}\Bigg(\prod_{i=1}^{h}p_{x_{i}}\times\prod_{(i,j)\in\mathsf{E}(H)}Q_{x_{i},x_{j}}\Bigg)\\
&=\sum_{K\subseteq\mathsf{V}(H)}p_{1}^{|K|}\times p_{2}^{|\mathsf{V}(H)|-|K|}\times Q_{1,1}^{|\mathsf{E}_{H}(K,K)|}Q_{1,2}^{|\mathsf{E}_{H}(K,\mathsf{V}(H)\backslash K)|}Q_{2,2}^{|\mathsf{E}_{H}(\mathsf{V}(H)\backslash K,\mathsf{V}(H)\backslash K)|},\end{split} $$

where the equivalence between the second and the third line follows simply by choosing $K$ to be the subset of vertices labeled by $1.$ In particular,

$$ \begin{split}&|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(H)|\\
&\leq\sum_{K\subseteq\mathsf{V}(H)}\Bigg|p_{1}^{|K|}\times p_{2}^{|\mathsf{V}(H)|-|K|}\times Q_{1,1}^{|\mathsf{E}_{H}(K,K)|}Q_{1,2}^{|\mathsf{E}_{H}(K,\mathsf{V}(H)\backslash K)|}Q_{2,2}^{|\mathsf{E}_{H}(\mathsf{V}(H)\backslash K,\mathsf{V}(H)\backslash K)|}\Bigg|\\
&\lesssim_{D}\max_{K\subseteq\mathsf{V}(H)}\Bigg|p_{1}^{|K|}\times Q_{1,1}^{|\mathsf{E}_{H}(K,K)|}Q_{1,2}^{|\mathsf{E}_{H}(K,\mathsf{V}(H)\backslash K)|}Q_{2,2}^{|\mathsf{E}_{H}(\mathsf{V}(H)\backslash K,\mathsf{V}(H)\backslash K)|}\Bigg|\\
&=\max_{K\subseteq\mathsf{V}(H)}p_{1}^{|K|}\times|Q_{1,1}|^{|\mathsf{E}_{H}(K,K)|}|Q_{1,2}|^{|\mathsf{E}_{H}(K,\mathsf{V}(H)\backslash K)|}|Q_{2,2}|^{|\mathsf{E}_{H}(\mathsf{V}(H)\backslash K,\mathsf{V}(H)\backslash K)|}\end{split} $$

From now on, we will focus on a specific choice of $K.$ Suppose that $K$ is such that $H|_{K}$ has $a$ connected components and $|K|=a+t.$ Hence, $|\mathsf{E}_{H}(K,K)|\geq t.$ Let $H|_{\mathsf{V}(H)\backslash K}$ have $b$ connected components and $b+s$ vertices. Hence, $|\mathsf{E}_{H}(\mathsf{V}(H)\backslash K,\mathsf{V}(H)\backslash K)|\geq s.$ Finally, observe that $|\mathsf{E}_{H}(K,\mathsf{V}(H)\backslash K)|\geq a+b-1$ since $H$ is connected.

Since $H$ is not a tree, $|\mathsf{E}(H)|\geq|\mathsf{V}(H)|=a+b+t+s.$ Thus, there is at least one more edge besides the $a+b+t+s-1$ identified so far. Suppose that it is of the type $|Q_{i,j}|.$ As in the layout from the end of Section 1.6.2, we aim to replace some of the $|Q_{1,2}|$ instances by $p_{1}|Q_{1,1}|$ so that we can compare to a 4-cycle. Namely:

$$ \begin{split}&p_{1}^{|K|}|Q_{1,1}|^{|\mathsf{E}_{H}(K,K)|}|Q_{1,2}|^{|\mathsf{E}_{H}(K,\mathsf{V}(H)\backslash K)|}|Q_{2,2}|^{|\mathsf{E}_{H}(\mathsf{V}(H)\backslash K,\mathsf{V}(H)\backslash K)|}\\
&\leq p_{1}^{a+t}\times|Q_{1,1}|^{t}\times|Q_{1,2}|^{a+b-1}\times|Q_{2,2}|^{s}\times|Q_{i,j}|\\
&\lesssim p_{1}^{a+t+a+b-1}\times|Q_{1,1}|^{a+b+t-1}\times|Q_{2,2}|^{s}\times|Q_{i,j}|,\end{split} $$

where we used Lemma 3.5 in the second inequality.

If $(i,j)\in\{(1,1),(1,2)\},$ then $a\geq 1$ (as label 1 exists) and $|Q_{i,j}|=O(|Q_{1,1}|).$ Thus, the above is expression is bounded by

$$ \displaystyle p_{1}^{a+b+t}\times|Q_{1,1}|^{a+b+t}\times|Q_{2,2}|^{s} \displaystyle\leq(p_{1}|Q_{1,1}|)^{a+b+t}\times|Q_{2,2}|^{s} \displaystyle\lesssim_{D}|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4})|^{\frac{a+b+t}{4}}\times|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4})|^{\frac{s}{4}} \displaystyle=|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4})|^{\frac{|\mathsf{V}(H)|}{4}}, $$

which completes the proof.

If $(i,j)=(2,2),$ the above expression is bounded by

$$ p_{1}^{t+a+b-1}\times|Q_{1,1}|^{a+b+t-1}\times|Q_{2,2}|^{s+1}. $$

We argue similarly that this is at most $\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4})|^{\frac{|\mathsf{V}(H)|}{4}}$ up to multiplicative constants depending on $D.$ ∎

If we were to apply the same argument when $H$ were a tree, we would prove that

$$ |\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(H)|\lesssim_{D}|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4})|^{\frac{|\mathsf{V}(H)|-1}{4}}, $$

which is not strong enough. Thus, we need to use the technique of isolating leaves as in Theorem 3.4

#### Proof of Lemma 3.6 when $H$ is a tree.

Now, suppose that $H$ is a tree. Again, there is nothing to prove if it has less than 3 vertices. If it has at least three vertices, then it has at least two leaves. Let these be $h-1$ and $h.$

We now bound $|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(H)|$ by using the same technique as in Theorem 3.4. Namely,

$$ \begin{split}&\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(H)\\
&=\sum_{K\subseteq\mathsf{V}(H)\backslash\{h-1,h\}}p^{|K|}Q_{1,1}^{|\mathsf{E}_{H}(K,K)|}Q_{1,2}^{|\mathsf{E}_{H}(K,\mathsf{V}(H)\backslash K)|}Q_{2,2}^{|E(\mathsf{V}(H)\backslash K,\mathsf{V}(H)\backslash K)|}\\
&\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\times(p_{1}Q_{1,1}+p_{2}Q_{1,2})^{P_{1}(K)}(p_{1}Q_{1,2}+p_{2}Q_{2,2})^{P_{2}(K)},\end{split} $$

where $P_{1}(K)$ is the number of parents of $h,h-1$ with label $1$ according to $K$ and $P_{2}(K)$ with label 2 (in case of a common parent, we count it twice). Note that $P_{1}(K)+P_{2}(K)=2.$ By AM-GM,

$$ \displaystyle|(p_{1}Q_{1,1}+p_{2}Q_{2,2})^{P_{1}(K)}(p_{1}Q_{1,2}+p_{2}Q_{2,2})^{P_{2}(K)}| \displaystyle\lesssim p_{1}^{-\mathds{1}[|K|\geq 1]}\Bigg(p_{1}(p_{1}Q_{1,1}+p_{2}Q_{1,2})^{2}+p_{2}(p_{1}Q_{1,2}+p_{2}Q_{2,2})^{2}\Bigg) \displaystyle=p_{1}^{-\mathds{1}[|K|\geq 1]}\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{2}). $$

The $\mathds{1}[|K|\geq 1]$ factor comes from the fact that if $|K|=0,$ then $P_{1}(K)=0.$ Combining with (37),

$$ \begin{split}&\Big|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(H)\Big|\\
&\lesssim_{D}\max_{K\subseteq\mathsf{V}(H)\backslash\{h,h-1\}}p^{|K|}|Q_{1,1}|^{|\mathsf{E}_{H}(K,K)|}|Q_{1,2}|^{|\mathsf{E}_{H}(K,H\backslash K)|}|Q_{2,2}|^{|\mathsf{E}_{H}(\mathsf{V}(H)\backslash K,\mathsf{V}(H)\backslash K)|}\\
&\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\times p^{-\mathds{1}[|K|\geq 1]}|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{2})|\end{split} $$

Again, we denote by $a$ the connected components of $K,$ by $a+t$ its vertices, by $b$ the connected components of $\mathsf{V}(H)\backslash K$ and by $b+s$ the number of vertices.

We rewrite the right hand-side of (38) as

$$ \displaystyle p_{1}^{a+t}|Q_{1,1}|^{t}|Q_{1,2}|^{a+b-1}|Q_{2,2}|^{s}p_{1}^{-\mathds{1}[a\geq 1]}|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{2})| \displaystyle\leq p_{1}^{a+t-1+a+b-\mathds{1}[a\geq 1]}|Q_{1,1}|^{a+b+t-1}|Q_{2,2}|^{s}|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{2})|, $$

where again the inequality follows from Lemma 3.5. Using that $a-\mathds{1}[a\geq 1]\geq 0,$ we continue as follows

$$ \displaystyle(p_{1}|Q_{1,1}|)^{a+b+t-1}|Q_{2,2}|^{s}|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{2})| \displaystyle\lesssim_{D}|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4})|^{\frac{a+b+t-1}{4}}|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4})|^{\frac{s}{4}}|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{2})| \displaystyle=|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4})|^{\frac{|V(H)|-3}{4}}|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{2})|. $$

Exactly as in the proof of Theorem 3.4, this implies that

$$ \Psi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(H)\lesssim_{D}\max\big(\Psi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4}),\Psi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{2})\big).\qed $$

#### 3.4.4 Step 4: Between-Community Cancellations.

Now, suppose that (30) holds in the case of between-community cancellations, (32). Additionally, we assume that $|Q_{1,2}|\geq p_{1}|Q_{1,1}|$ as otherwise we can invoke Lemma 3.6 and complete the proof. In particular, $p_{1}|Q_{1,1}|+p_{2}|Q_{1,2}|\leq 2|Q_{1,2}|.$ By (32), also $|p_{1}Q_{1,1}+p_{2}Q_{1,2}|\geq\frac{p_{2}}{C}|Q_{1,2}|\geq\frac{1}{2C}|Q_{1,2}|.$ We record:

$$ \displaystyle\frac{1}{2C}|Q_{1,2}|\leq|p_{1}Q_{1,1}+p_{2}Q_{1,2}|\leq 2|Q_{1,2}| $$

Furthermore, (32) implies that $p_{1}(p_{1}Q_{1,1}+p_{2}Q_{1,2})^{\mathbf{T}},p_{2}(p_{1}Q_{1,2}+p_{2}Q_{2,2})^{\mathbf{T}}$ have different signs. In particular, $\mathbf{T}$ is odd. Hence, $\mathbf{T}\leq D-1$ as $D$ is even.

Next, we will show that unless $p_{1}\geq|Q_{1,2}|,$ $\mathsf{Star}_{\mathbf{T}+1}$ dominates $H.$

#### Lemma 3.7.

Suppose that (30) holds and $p_{1}\leq|Q_{1,2}|.$ Then,

$$ \Psi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(H)\lesssim_{D}\Psi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{\mathbf{T}+1}) $$

#### Proof.

For brevity, denote $\mu=p_{1}Q_{1,1}+p_{2}Q_{1,2},\lambda=p_{1}Q_{1,2}+p_{2}Q_{2,2}.$ When (32) holds, $C|\mu|\geq p_{1}|Q_{1,1}|+p_{2}|Q_{1,2}|$ and $C|\lambda|\geq p_{1}|Q_{1,2}|+p_{2}|Q_{2,2}|.$ However, $(4C^{2})^{\mathbf{T}}\times|p_{1}\mu^{\mathbf{T}}+p_{2}\lambda^{\mathbf{T}}|\leq\Big(p_{1}|\mu|^{\mathbf{T}}+p_{2}|\lambda|^{\mathbf{T}}\Big).$ In particular, this means $(4C^{2})^{\mathbf{T}}\times\Big|p_{1}|\mu|^{\mathbf{T}}-p_{2}|\lambda|^{\mathbf{T}}\Big|\leq\Big(p_{1}|\mu|^{\mathbf{T}}+p_{2}|\lambda|^{\mathbf{T}}\Big),$ so $p_{1}|\mu|^{\mathbf{T}}\in(1\pm 1/2)p_{2}|\lambda|^{\mathbf{T}}$ when $C\geq 4.$ By (39), also $|\mu|\geq\frac{1}{2C}|Q_{1,2}|\geq\frac{p_{1}}{2C}.$

Now, since $\mathbf{T}+1$ is even and $\mu\geq\frac{p_{1}}{2C},$ $(p_{1}\mu^{\mathbf{T}+1})^{1/(\mathbf{T}+2)}\gtrsim_{D}(p_{1}|\mu|^{\mathbf{T}})^{1/(\mathbf{T}+1)}.$ Altogether,

$$ \displaystyle|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{\mathbf{T}+1})|^{\frac{1}{|\mathsf{V}(\mathsf{Star}_{\mathbf{T}+1})|}}=|p_{1}\mu^{\mathbf{T}+1}+p_{2}\lambda^{\mathbf{T}+1}|^{1/(\mathbf{T}+2)}\geq|p_{1}\mu^{\mathbf{T}+1}|^{1/(\mathbf{T}+2)}\gtrsim_{D}|p_{1}\mu^{\mathbf{T}}|^{1/(\mathbf{T}+1)} \displaystyle\gtrsim_{D}\big(p_{1}|\mu|^{\mathbf{T}}+p_{2}|\lambda|^{\mathbf{T}}\big)^{1/(\mathbf{T}+1)}=|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,|Q|)}(\mathsf{Star}_{\mathbf{T}})|^{1/(\mathbf{T}+1)}\gtrsim_{D}|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(H)|^{\frac{1}{|\mathsf{V}(H)|}}.\qed $$

Thus, from now on, we

$$ \displaystyle\text{ Assume that }|Q_{1,2}|\leq p_{1}. $$

#### Lemma 3.8.

Suppose that (30) holds, $|Q_{1,2}|\leq p_{1},$ and $\mathbf{T}>1.$ Then,

$$ \Psi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(H)\lesssim_{D}\Psi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{\mathbf{T}-1}) $$

#### Proof sketch.

The proof is exactly the same as that of Lemma 3.8. The only difference is that this time $|\mu|\lesssim_{D}p_{1},$ which implies $(p_{1}\mu^{\mathbf{T}-1})^{1/\mathbf{T}}\gtrsim_{D}(p_{1}|\mu|^{\mathbf{T}})^{1/(\mathbf{T}+1)}.$ ∎

Hence, what is left is the case $\mathbf{T}=1.$ For convenience, we restate and recall the conditions in the remaining case:

- 1. $\mathbf{T}=1.$

- 2. (32): $p_{1}|Q_{1,1}|+p_{2}|Q_{1,2}|\leq C\times|pQ_{1,1}+p_{2}Q_{1,2}|,$ and $p_{1}|Q_{1,2}|+p_{2}|Q_{2,2}|\leq C\times|p_{1}Q_{1,2}+p_{2}Q_{2,2}|,$ and $\displaystyle(4C^{2})\times|p_{1}(p_{1}Q_{1,1}+p_{2}Q_{1,2})+p_{2}(p_{1}Q_{1,2}+p_{2}Q_{2,2})|\leq p_{1}|p_{1}Q_{1,1}+p_{2}Q_{1,2}|+p_{2}|pQ_{1,2}+p_{2}Q_{2,2}|.$

- 3. $|Q_{1,2}|\geq p_{1}|Q_{1,1}|$ as otherwise Lemma 3.6 gives Theorem 3.6.

- 4. $|Q_{2,2}|\leq 8cp_{1}|Q_{1,2}|$ for large enough $C.$

- 5. For any even $t\in[2,D],$

Using that $|Q_{2,2}|\leq p_{1}|Q_{1,2}|,$ the above expression is bounded by

$$ \displaystyle p_{1}^{a+t+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|}|Q_{1,1}|^{t}|Q_{1,2}|^{a+b-1+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|}|p_{1}Q_{1,1}+Q_{1,2}|^{|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|}. $$

We now analyze two cases based on which of the two quantities $|Q_{1,1}|\sqrt{p_{1}}$ and $|Q_{1,2}|$ is larger. Again, the intuition is as in Section 1.6.2 – this will allow us to replace instances of $|Q_{1,2}|$ with $|Q_{1,1}|\sqrt{p_{1}}$ and compare witha four-cycle.

#### Case 1) $|Q_{1,1}|\sqrt{p_{1}}\leq|Q_{1,2}|.$

Using $|Q_{1,1}|\sqrt{p_{1}}\leq|Q_{1,2}|$ , we bound (44) by

$$ \displaystyle p_{1}^{a+t/2+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|}|Q_{1,2}|^{a+b-1+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+t}|p_{1}Q_{1,1}+Q_{1,2}|^{|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|}. $$

#### Case 1.1) $|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|\leq 2.$

Using that $p_{1}|Q_{1,1}|\leq|Q_{1,2}|,$ the expression in (45) is bounded by

$$ \displaystyle p_{1}^{a+t/2+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|}|\times|Q_{1,2}|^{a+b-1+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+t+|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|} \displaystyle\lesssim p_{1}^{a+t/2+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|-1}|\times|Q_{1,2}|^{a+b-3+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+t+|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|}\times\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{2}) $$

where we used (42).

#### Case 1.1.1)

Now, suppose that

$$ a+t/2+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|-1\geq\frac{1}{2}(a+b-3+s+t+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|)=\frac{1}{2}(|\mathsf{V}(H)|-3). $$

Then, using Claim 3.4, the above expression is bounded by

$$ \displaystyle(\sqrt{p_{1}}|Q_{1,2}|)^{a+b-3+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+t+|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|}\times\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{2}) \displaystyle\lesssim|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4})|^{\frac{|\mathsf{V}(H)|-3}{4}}\times|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{2})|. $$

As in Theorem 3.3, this expression is at most

$$ \max(|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4})|^{1/4},|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{2})|^{1/3})^{|V(H)|}. $$

#### Case 1.1.2)

The remaining case is

$$ \displaystyle a+t/2+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|-1<\frac{1}{2}(a+b-3+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+t+|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|)\quad\quad\quad\Longleftrightarrow \displaystyle a+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+1<b+|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|\quad\quad\quad\Longleftrightarrow \displaystyle a+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+2\leq b+|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|. $$

Since $|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|\leq 2$ in the current case, it follows that $b=a+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+r$ for some $r\geq 0.$ Under these assumptions, we prove the following fact.

#### Claim 3.9.

$H|_{\mathsf{V}(H)\backslash(K\cup\mathsf{L}_{1}(K))}$ has at least $R\geq b-s-|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|=a+r$ isolated vertices.

#### Proof.

Indeed, note that $H|_{\mathsf{V}(H)\backslash(K\cup\mathsf{L}(H))}$ has $b$ connected components and $b+s$ vertices. Hence, at least $b-s$ of the vertices in $H|_{\mathsf{V}(H)\backslash(K\cup\mathsf{L}(H))}$ are isolated. These same vertices are not isolated in $H|_{\mathsf{V}(H)\backslash(K\cup\mathsf{L}_{1}(K))}$ if and only if they have a neighbor in $\mathsf{L}_{2}(K).$ As each vertex in $\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)$ is a leaf, there are at most $|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|$ such of them. Hence, at least $b-s-|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|=a+r$ of the vertices in $\mathsf{V}(H)\backslash(K\cup\mathsf{L}(H))$ are isolated in $H|_{\mathsf{V}(H)\backslash(K\cup|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|)}.$ ∎

Denote these isolated vertices by $\mathcal{S},$ so $|\mathcal{S}|\geq a+r.$ Now consider $H|_{V(H)\backslash\mathsf{L}(H)}.$ This is a connected graph since $H$ is connected and $\mathsf{L}(H)$ is the set of leaves. Hence, each connected component in $H|_{V(H)\backslash(K\cup\mathsf{L}(H))}$ has at least one edge to a vertex in $K.$ If, furthermore, this connected component is one of the vertices in $\mathcal{S},$ it must have at least $2$ edges to $K.$ At least one edge due to connectivity and at least one more as the vertices of $\mathcal{S}$ are not leaves. Indeed, note that $\mathcal{S}\subseteq\mathsf{V}(H)\backslash(K\cup\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)$ ) and they don’t have any edges to other vertices in $\mathsf{V}(H)\backslash(K\cup\mathsf{L}_{1}(K))$ due to being isolated, and in $\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)$ due to the fact that the parents of leaves in $\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)$ are all in $K.$ Altogether, this means that the number of edges between $K$ and $\mathsf{V}(H)\backslash(\mathsf{L}(H)\cup K)$ is at least

$$ 2|\mathcal{S}|+(b-|\mathcal{S}|)\geq b+|\mathcal{S}|\geq b+a+r. $$

Note that all of these edges are of type $(1,2).$ Thus, the bound in (43) becomes

$$ \begin{split}&|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(H)|\\
&\lesssim_{D}p_{1}^{a+t}|Q_{1,1}|^{t}\times|Q_{1,2}|^{b+a+r}\times|Q_{2,2}|^{s}\times|p_{1}Q_{1,1}+p_{2}Q_{1,2}|^{|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|}|p_{1}Q_{1,2}+p_{2}Q_{2,2}|^{|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|}\\
&\quad\quad\quad\quad\text{(Using that $\sqrt{p_{1}}|Q_{1,1}|\leq|Q_{1,2}|,p_{1}|Q_{1,2}|\gtrsim|Q_{2,2}|$ and \lx@cref{creftypeplural~refnum}{eq:boundonpbeta11plusbeta22} and\lx@nobreakspace\lx@cref{refnum}{eq:insecondcommunity12dominates})}\\
&\lesssim_{D}p_{1}^{a+t}|Q_{1,2}|^{t}p^{-t/2}|Q_{1,2}|^{b+a+r}\times|Q_{1,2}|^{s}p^{s}|Q_{1,2}|^{|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|}|Q_{1,2}|^{|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|}p_{1}^{|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|}\\
&\lesssim_{D}p_{1}^{a+t/2+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|}|Q_{1,2}|^{t+b+a+r+s+|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|}\\
&\lesssim p_{1}^{a+t/2+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|-1}\times|Q_{1,2}|^{t+b+a+s+|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|-3}\times p_{1}|Q_{1,2}|^{2}\times|Q_{1,2}|^{1+r}\\
&\quad\quad\quad\quad\text{(Using that $|Q_{1,2}|\leq p_{1}.$)}\\
&\lesssim p_{1}^{a+t/2+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+r}\times|Q_{1,2}|^{t+b+a+s+|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|-3}\times p_{1}|Q_{1,2}|^{2},\end{split} $$

Now, observe that

$$ a+t/2+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+r\geq\frac{1}{2}(t+b+a+s+|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|-3) $$

since this is equivalent to

$$ a+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+2r+3\geq b+|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|, $$

but $a+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+r=b,r+3\geq 3>|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|.$ Altogether, the above expression is bounded by the familiar

$$ (\sqrt{p_{1}}|Q_{1,2}|)^{t+b+a+s+|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|-3}\times p_{1}|Q_{1,2}|^{2}\lesssim|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4})|^{\frac{|\mathsf{V}(H)|-3}{4}}\times|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{2})|, $$

where the inequality follows from 3.4 and 42.

#### Case 1.2) $|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|\geq 3.$

Let $\xi\in\{0,1\}$ be such that $|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|-\xi$ is even. We bound (43) by

$$ \displaystyle p_{1}^{a+t+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|}|Q_{1,1}|^{t}|Q_{1,2}|^{a+b-1+s}|p_{1}Q_{1,1}+p_{2}Q_{1,2}|^{|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|}\times|p_{1}Q_{1,2}+p_{2}Q_{2,2}|^{|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|} \sqrt{p_{1}}|Q_{1,1}|\leq|Q_{1,2}| \displaystyle\lesssim_{D}p_{1}^{a+t+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|}|Q_{1,2}|^{t}p^{-t/2}|Q_{1,2}|^{a+b-1+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|}|p_{1}Q_{1,1}+p_{2}Q_{1,2}|^{|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|-\xi}|Q_{1,2}|^{\xi} \displaystyle\lesssim_{D}p_{1}^{a+t/2+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|}|Q_{1,2}|^{a+b-1+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+t+\xi}|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|-\xi})|. $$

Again, we consider two cases.

#### Case 1.2.1)

If

$$ \displaystyle a+t/2+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|\geq\frac{1}{2}(a+b-1+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+t+\xi)\quad\quad\quad\Longleftrightarrow \displaystyle a+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|\geq b+\xi-1, $$

the last expression is bounded by

$$ \displaystyle(\sqrt{p_{1}}|Q_{1,2}|)^{a+b-1+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+t+\xi}|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|-\xi})| \displaystyle\lesssim|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4})|^{\frac{|V(H)|-|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|-1+\xi}{4}}|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|-\xi})| \displaystyle\leq\max(|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4})|^{1/4},|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|-\xi})|^{1/(|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|-\xi+1)})^{|\mathsf{V}(H)|}. $$

The last inequality follows in the same way as for 2-stars and 4-cycles as in Theorem 3.3.

#### Case 1.2.2)

Otherwise,

$$ \displaystyle a+t/2+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|<\frac{1}{2}(a+b-1+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+t+\xi)\quad\quad\quad\Longleftrightarrow \displaystyle a+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|<b+\xi-1, $$

so $b+\xi\geq a+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+2.$ Again, let $b+\xi=a+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+r$ for some $r\geq 2.$ We use the same argument as in Case 1) to argue that there are at least $b+a+r-\xi$ edges between $K$ and $\mathsf{V}(H)\backslash(K\cup\mathsf{L}(H)).$ We bound (43) by

$$ \begin{split}&|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(H)|\\
&\lesssim_{D}p_{1}^{a+t}|Q_{1,1}|^{t}\times|Q_{1,2}|^{b+a+r-\xi}\times|Q_{2,2}|^{s}\times|p_{1}Q_{1,1}+p_{2}Q_{1,2}|^{|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|}|p_{1}Q_{1,2}+p_{2}Q_{2,2}|^{|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|}\\
&\quad\quad\quad\quad\text{(Using $|Q_{1,1}|\sqrt{p_{1}}\leq|Q_{1,2}|,|Q_{2,2}|\leq p_{1}|Q_{1,2}|$ and \eqref{eq:starexpectationsint1outbrackets})}\\
&\lesssim p_{1}^{a+t}|Q_{1,2}|^{t}p_{1}^{-t/2}|Q_{1,2}|^{b+a+r-\xi}\times|Q_{1,2}|^{s}p^{s}\\
&\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\times p^{-1}|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|-\xi})|\times|Q_{1,2}|^{\xi}|Q_{1,2}|^{|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|}p_{1}^{|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|}\\
&\lesssim p_{1}^{a+t/2+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|-1}|Q_{1,2}|^{t+b+a+r+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|}\times|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|-\xi})|\\
&\quad\quad\quad\quad\text{(Using $|Q_{1,2}|\leq p_{1}$)}\\
&\lesssim p_{1}^{a+t/2+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+r-\xi}|Q_{1,2}|^{t+b+a+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+\xi-1}\times|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|-\xi})|.\end{split} $$

Now, observe that

$$ \displaystyle a+t/2+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+r-\xi\geq\frac{1}{2}(t+b+a+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+\xi-1)\quad\quad\quad\Longleftrightarrow \displaystyle a+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+2r+1\geq b+3\xi, $$

but $b+\xi=a+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+r$ and $r+1\geq 3\geq 2\xi.$ Altogether, this means that the above expression is at most

$$ \displaystyle(\sqrt{p_{1}}|Q_{1,2}|)^{t+b+a+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+\xi-1}\times|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|-\xi})| \displaystyle\leq|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4})|^{\frac{|V(H)|-|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|-1+\xi}{4}}\times|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|-\xi})|. $$

Again, this is enough.

#### Case 2) $|Q_{1,1}|\sqrt{p_{1}}>|Q_{1,2}|$

We consider the same two cases based on $|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|.$

#### Case 2.1) $|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|\leq 2.$

We bound the expression in (43) by

$$ \displaystyle p_{1}^{a+t+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|}|Q_{1,1}|^{t}|Q_{1,2}|^{a+b-1+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|}|p_{1}Q_{1,1}+p_{2}Q_{1,2}|^{|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|} \displaystyle\lesssim_{D}p_{1}^{a+t+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|}|Q_{1,1}|^{t}\times|Q_{1,2}|^{a+b-1+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|}\times|Q_{1,2}|^{|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|} {p_{1}}\geq|Q_{1,2}| \displaystyle\lesssim_{D}p_{1}^{a+t+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|-1}\times|Q_{1,1}|^{t}\times|Q_{1,2}|^{a+b+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|-3}\times p_{1}|Q_{1,2}|^{2} \sqrt{p_{1}}|Q_{1,1}|>|Q_{1,2}| \displaystyle\lesssim_{D}p_{1}^{a+t+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|-1}\times|Q_{1,1}|^{t}\times|Q_{1,1}|^{a+b+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|-3}p^{(a+b+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|-3)/2}\times p_{1}|Q_{1,2}|^{2} \displaystyle\lesssim_{D}p_{1}^{a+t+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|-1+\frac{1}{2}(a+b+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|-3)}|Q_{1,1}|^{t+a+b+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|-3}\times\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{2}). $$

#### Case 2.1.1)

If

$$ \displaystyle a+t+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|-1+\frac{1}{2}(a+b+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|-3)\geq \displaystyle\quad\quad\quad\quad\geq t+a+b+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|-3\Longleftrightarrow \displaystyle a+s+\mathsf{L}_{2}+1\geq b+\mathsf{L}_{1}, $$

then going back we have

$$ \displaystyle p^{a+t+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|-1+\frac{1}{2}(a+b+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|-3)}|Q_{1,1}|^{t+a+b+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|-3}\times\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{2}) \displaystyle\leq(p_{1}|Q_{1,1}|)^{|V(H)|-3}\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{2}) \displaystyle\leq\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4})^{\frac{|V(H)|-3}{4}}\times\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{2}) \displaystyle\leq\max(|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4})|^{1/4},|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{2})|^{1/3})^{|V(H)|}. $$

#### Case 2.1.2)

Otherwise, $a+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+1<b+|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|\leq b+2,$ so $b=a+s+\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)+r,$ where $r\geq 0.$ Again, using the argument of counting isolated vertices, we lower-bound the number of edges between $K$ and $\mathsf{V}(H)\backslash(K\cup\mathsf{L}(H))$ by $a+b+r,$ so

$$ \begin{split}&|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(H)|\\
&\quad\quad\quad\quad\text{(By \eqref{eq:trianglineqcrosscommunity})}\\
&\lesssim_{D}p_{1}^{a+t}|Q_{1,1}|^{t}\times|Q_{1,2}|^{b+a+r}\times|Q_{2,2}|^{s}\times|p_{1}Q_{1,1}+p_{2}Q_{1,2}|^{|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|}|p_{1}Q_{1,2}+p_{2}Q_{2,2}|^{|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|}\\
&\quad\quad\quad\quad\text{(Using that $\sqrt{p_{1}}|Q_{1,1}|>|Q_{1,2}|$)}\\
&\lesssim p_{1}^{a+t}|Q_{1,1}|^{t}\times|Q_{1,2}|^{b+a+r}\times|Q_{1,2}|^{s}p^{s}\times|Q_{1,2}|^{|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|}|Q_{1,2}|^{|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|}p_{1}^{|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|}\\
&\lesssim p_{1}^{a+t+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|}\times|Q_{1,1}|^{t}\times|Q_{1,2}|^{b+a+r+s+|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|}\\
&\quad\quad\quad\quad\text{(Using that $p_{1}>|Q_{1,2}|$)}\\
&\lesssim p_{1}^{a+t+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+r}|Q_{1,1}|^{t}\times|Q_{1,2}|^{b+a+s+|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|}\\
&\quad\quad\quad\quad\text{(Using that $p_{1}>|Q_{1,2}|$)}\\
&\lesssim p_{1}^{a+t+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+r}|Q_{1,1}|^{t}\times|Q_{1,2}|^{b+a+s+|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|-3}p_{1}|Q_{1,2}|^{2}\\
&\quad\quad\quad\quad\text{(Using \eqref{eq:starexpectationsint1outbrackets})}\\
&\lesssim p_{1}^{a+t+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+r+\frac{1}{2}(b+a+s+|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|-3)}|Q_{1,1}|^{t+b+a+s+|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|-3}p_{1}|Q_{1,2}|^{2}.\\
\end{split} $$

Now, observe that

$$ \displaystyle a+t+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+r+\frac{1}{2}(b+a+s+|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|-3)\geq \displaystyle\quad\quad\quad\quad\geq t+b+a+s+|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|-3\quad\quad\quad\Longleftrightarrow \displaystyle 3+2r+a+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|\geq b+\mathsf{L}_{1}. $$

This inequality holds as $r+a+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|\geq b,3+r\geq 3\geq|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|.$ Hence, the last expression in (46) is bounded by

$$ (p_{1}|Q_{1,1}|)^{t+b+a+s+|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|-3}p_{1}|Q_{1,2}|^{2}\lesssim|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4})|^{\frac{|V(H)|-3}{4}}\times|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{2})|. $$

#### Case 2.2) $|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|>2.$

Let $\xi\in\{0,1\}$ be such that $|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|-\xi$ is even. Then, we bound the expression in (43) by

$$ \displaystyle p_{1}^{a+t+s}|Q_{1,1}|^{t}|Q_{1,2}|^{a+b-1+s}|p_{1}Q_{1,2}+p_{2}Q_{2,2}|^{|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|}|p_{1}Q_{1,1}+p_{2}Q_{1,2}|^{|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|} \displaystyle\lesssim_{D}p_{1}^{a+t+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|}|Q_{1,1}|^{t}|Q_{1,2}|^{a+b-1+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|}|p_{1}Q_{1,1}+p_{2}Q_{1,2}|^{|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|} \displaystyle\lesssim_{D}p_{1}^{a+t+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|-1}|Q_{1,1}|^{t}\times|Q_{1,2}|^{a+b-1+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|}\times p_{1}|p_{1}Q_{1,1}+p_{2}Q_{1,2}|^{|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|-\xi}|\times|Q_{1,2}|^{\xi} \displaystyle\lesssim p_{1}^{a+t+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|-1}|Q_{1,1}|^{t}\times|Q_{1,2}|^{a+b-1+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+\xi}\times|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|-\xi})| \sqrt{p_{1}}|Q_{1,1}|>|Q_{1,2}| \displaystyle\lesssim p_{1}^{a+t+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|-1}|Q_{1,1}|^{t}\times|Q_{1,1}|^{a+b-1+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+\xi}p_{1}^{\frac{1}{2}(a+b-1+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+\xi)}\times|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|-\xi})| \displaystyle\lesssim p_{1}^{a+t+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|-1+\frac{1}{2}(a+b-1+s+(K)+\xi)}|Q_{1,1}|^{t+a+b-1+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+\xi}\times|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|-\xi})|. $$

#### Case 2.2.1)

If

$$ \displaystyle a+t+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|-1+\frac{1}{2}(a+b-1+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+\xi) \displaystyle\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\geq t+a+b-1+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+\xi\quad\quad\quad\Longleftrightarrow \displaystyle a-1+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|\geq b+\xi, $$

the above expression is at most

$$ \displaystyle(p_{1}|Q_{1,1}|)^{t+a+b-1+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+\xi}\times|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|-\xi})| \displaystyle\lesssim|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4})|^{\frac{|V(H)|-|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|-1+\xi}{4}}\times|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|-\xi})|\leq \displaystyle\leq\max(|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4})|^{1/4},|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|-\xi})|^{1/(|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|-\xi+1)})^{|V(H)|}. $$

#### Case 2.2.2)

Otherwise, $a-1+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|<b+\xi,$ so $b+\xi=a+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+r,$ where $r\geq 0.$ Using the isolated-vertices argument, there are at least $b+a+r-\xi$ edges between $K$ and $\mathsf{V}(H)\backslash(K\cup\mathsf{L}(H)).$ We bound (43) as

$$ \begin{split}&|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(H)|\\
&\lesssim_{D}p_{1}^{a+t}|Q_{1,1}|^{t}\times|Q_{1,2}|^{b+a+r-\xi}\times|Q_{2,2}|^{s}\times|p_{1}Q_{1,1}+p_{2}Q_{1,2}|^{|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|}|p_{1}Q_{1,2}+p_{2}Q_{2,2}|^{|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|}\\
&\quad\quad\quad\quad\text{(Using ${p_{1}}|Q_{1,2}|\gtrsim|Q_{2,2}|$) and \eqref{eq:boundonpbeta11plusbeta22} and \eqref{eq:insecondcommunity12dominates}}\\
&\lesssim p_{1}^{a+t}|Q_{1,1}|^{t}|Q_{1,2}|^{b+a+r-\xi}\times|Q_{1,2}|^{s}p_{1}^{s}p_{1}^{-1}\times\\
&\quad\quad\quad\quad\times p_{1}|p_{1}Q_{1,1}+p_{2}Q_{1,2}|^{|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|-\xi}\times|p_{1}Q_{1,1}+p_{2}Q_{1,2}|^{\xi}|Q_{1,2}|^{|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|}p_{1}^{|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|}\\
&\quad\quad\quad\quad\text{(Using \eqref{eq:starexpectationsint1outbrackets})}\\
&\lesssim p_{1}^{a+t}|Q_{1,1}|^{t}|Q_{1,2}|^{b+a+r-\xi}\times|Q_{1,2}|^{s}p_{1}^{s}p_{1}^{-1}|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|-\xi})|\times|Q_{1,2}|^{|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+\xi}p_{1}^{|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|}\\
&\lesssim p_{1}^{a+t+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|-1}\times|Q_{1,1}|^{t}\times|Q_{1,2}|^{b+a+r+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|}\times|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|-\xi})|\\
&\quad\quad\quad\quad\text{(Using $p_{1}\geq|Q_{1,2}|$)}\\
&\lesssim p_{1}^{a+t+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|-1}\times|Q_{1,1}|^{t}\times|Q_{1,2}|^{b+a+r+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|-3}\times p_{1}Q_{1,2}^{2}\times|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|-\xi})|\\
&\quad\quad\quad\quad\text{(Using \eqref{eq:starexpectationsint1outbrackets})}\\
&\lesssim p_{1}^{a+t+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|-1}\times|Q_{1,1}|^{t}\times|Q_{1,2}|^{b+a+r+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|-3}\times|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{2})|\times|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|-\xi})|\\
&\quad\quad\quad\quad\text{(Using $p_{1}\geq|Q_{1,2}|$)}\\
&\lesssim p_{1}^{a+t+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|-1+1+r-\xi}\times|Q_{1,1}|^{t}\times|Q_{1,2}|^{b+a+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|-4+\xi}\times\\
&\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{2})|\times|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|-\xi})|\\
&\quad\quad\quad\quad\text{(Using $\sqrt{p_{1}}|Q_{1,1}|\geq|Q_{1,2}|$)}\\
&\lesssim p_{1}^{a+t+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+r-\xi}\times|Q_{1,1}|^{t+b+a+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|-4+\xi}\times p_{1}^{\frac{1}{2}(b+a+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|-4+\xi)}\times\\
&\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{2})|\times|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|-\xi})|\\
&\lesssim p_{1}^{a+t+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+r-\xi+\frac{1}{2}(b+a+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|-4+\xi)}\times|Q_{1,1}|^{t+b+a+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|-4+\xi}\times\\
&\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{2})|\times|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|-\xi})|.\\
\end{split} $$

Now, observe that

$$ \displaystyle a+t+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+r-\xi+\frac{1}{2}(b+a+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|-4+\xi)\geq \displaystyle\quad\quad\quad\quad\geq t+b+a+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|-4+\xi\quad\quad\quad\Longleftrightarrow \displaystyle 2r+a+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|+4\geq 3\xi+b, $$

which is true since $b+\xi=r+a+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|,2\xi\leq 4.$ Furthermore,

$$ t+b+a+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|-4+\xi=|\mathsf{V}(H)\backslash\mathsf{L}(K)|+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|-4+\xi\geq 1+3-4\geq 0, $$

since $|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|\geq 3$ in case 2.2) and $|\mathsf{V}(H)\backslash\mathsf{L}(K)|\geq 1$ as $H$ is connected and has at least 3 leaves and any such graph has a non-leaf vertex, and $\xi\geq 0$ by definition.

Altogether, (47) is bounded by

$$ \displaystyle(p_{1}|Q_{1,1}|)^{t+b+a+s+|\mathsf{L}_{2}(K)|-4+\xi}\times|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{2})|\times|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|-\xi})| \displaystyle\lesssim_{D}|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4})|^{\frac{|V(H)|+\xi-|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|-4}{4}}\times|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{2})|\times|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|-\xi})| \displaystyle=\Bigg(|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4})|^{1/4}\Bigg)^{|V(H)|+\xi-|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|-4}\times\Bigg(|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{2})|^{1/3}\Bigg)^{3} \displaystyle\quad\quad\quad\times\bigg(|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|-\xi})|^{1/(|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|-\xi+1)}\Bigg)^{|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|-\xi+1} \displaystyle\leq\max\Big(\Psi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4}),\Psi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{2}),\Psi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{|\mathsf{L}_{1}(K)|-\xi})\Big)^{|\mathsf{V}(H)|}. $$

With this, the proof of Theorem 3.6 is complete.∎

#### 3.4.5 Testing in 2-SBMs

#### Theorem 3.7 (Testing in 2-SBMs).

Suppose that $\mathbb{SBM}(n;p,Q)$ is a stochastic block-model on two communities such that $\min(p_{1},p_{2})=\omega(1/n).$ Suppose that there exists a polynomial test of degree at most $D,$ for some even absolute constant $D\geq 4,$ distinguishing $\mathbb{SBM}(n;p,Q)$ and ${\mathbb{G}(n,1/2)}$ with high probability. Then, one can also distinguish the two graph distribution with high probability via either the signed 4-cycle count or the signed count of a star on at most $D$ edges.

#### Remark 1.

The condition $\min(p_{1},p_{2})=\omega(1/n)$ is very minimal. Suppose that $p_{1}\leq p_{2}.$ If $\min(p_{1},p_{2})=o(1/n),$ so $p_{1}=o(1/n),$ then with high probability, there is no vertex of label 1, so $\mathbb{SBM}(n;p,Q)$ is (in total variation) close to $\mathbb{G}(n,(Q_{2,2}+1)/2).$ Trivially, the signed edge count is an optimal distinguisher between $\mathbb{G}(n,q)$ and ${\mathbb{G}(n,1/2)}$ for any $q.$ If $p_{1}=\Theta(1/n),$ then we can prove a slightly weaker result by blowing up the “vertex-sample complexity” as in Definition 3. Namely, the result we will prove is that if there exists a polynomial test of degree at most $D$ for some even $D\geq 4$ distinguishing $\mathbb{SBM}(n;p,Q)$ and ${\mathbb{G}(n,1/2)},$ then one can distinguish $\mathbb{SBM}(N(n);p,Q)$ and $\mathbb{G}(N(n),1/2)$ via either the signed 4-cycle count or the signed count of a star on at most $D$ edges, where $N(n)$ is any function that satisfies $N(n)=\omega(n).$ The idea is that if $N(n)=\omega(n)$ and $p_{1}=\Theta(1/n),$ then $p_{1}=\omega(1/N(n)).$

#### Proof.

By Theorem 3.6, we know that for any graph on at most $D$ edges without isolated vertices,

$$ \Psi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(H)\lesssim_{D}\max\Bigg(\Psi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4}),\max_{1\leq t\leq D}\Psi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{t})\Bigg). $$

If an approximate maximum on the right hand-side above is achieved by a 4-cycle or a star on at most $D/2$ edges, the conclusion follows by Theorem 2.4. Suppose instead that the maximum is achieved by some $\mathsf{Star}_{t}$ such that $t\in\{D/2+1,\ldots,D\}.$

#### Step 1: Identifying relationships between $p,Q.$

As in the proof of Theorem 3.6, we first identify several relationships between $p$ and $Q.$

First, from Theorem 2.3,

$$ \displaystyle\Psi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{t})=\omega(n^{-1/2}). $$

Second, it implies that $\mathsf{Star}_{2}$ is not an approximate maximizer, so

$$ \displaystyle\Psi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{3})=o(\Psi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{t})). $$

Without loss of generality, let $p_{1}\leq p_{2}.$ Let also $\lambda_{i}\coloneqq p_{1}Q_{1,i}+p_{2}Q_{2,i},$ so $\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{r})=p_{1}\lambda_{1}^{r}+p_{2}\lambda_{2}^{r}.$ Now, (49) implies that

$$ \displaystyle(p_{1}\lambda_{1}^{2}+p_{2}\lambda_{2}^{2})^{1/3}=o\Big((p_{1}\lambda_{1}^{t}+p_{2}\lambda_{2}^{t})^{1/(t+1)}\Big)\Longrightarrow \displaystyle(p_{1}\lambda_{1}^{2}+p_{2}\lambda_{2}^{2})^{(t+1)}=o\Big((p_{1}|\lambda_{1}|^{t}+p_{2}|\lambda_{2}|^{t})^{3}\Big)\Longrightarrow \displaystyle p_{1}^{t+1}|\lambda_{1}|^{2(t+1)}+p_{2}^{t+1}|\lambda_{2}|^{2(t+1)}=o\Big(p_{1}^{3}|\lambda_{1}|^{3t}+p_{2}^{3}|\lambda_{2}|^{3t}\Big). $$

Now, one of the following two systems of inequalities needs to be satisfied

- 1. $p_{2}^{t+1}|\lambda_{2}|^{2(t+1)}=o(p_{2}^{3}|\lambda_{2}|^{3t})$ and $p_{2}^{3}|\lambda_{2}|^{3t}\geq p_{1}^{3}|\lambda_{1}|^{3t}.$ Then, as $t=O(1),$ the first inequality implies that $p_{2}^{t-2}=o(|\lambda_{2}|^{t-2}).$ Thus,

$$ p_{2}=o(|\lambda_{2}|)=o(|p_{1}Q_{1,2}+p_{2}Q_{2,2}|)=o(p_{1}|Q_{1,2}|+p_{2}|Q_{2,2}|)=o(2p_{2}), $$

contradiction. We used that $p_{1}\leq p_{2}$ and $|Q_{i,j}|\leq 1.$

- 2. $p_{1}^{t+1}|\lambda_{1}|^{2(t+1)}=o(p_{1}^{3}|\lambda_{1}|^{3t})$ and $p_{1}^{3}|\lambda_{1}|^{3t}\geq p_{2}^{3}|\lambda_{2}|^{3t}.$ As in the previous case, the first inequality implies that $p_{1}=o(|\lambda_{1}|).$ The second implies that $|\lambda_{1}|\geq|\lambda_{2}|$ as $p_{1}\leq p_{2}.$

Altogether, we have learned that:

$$ \displaystyle p_{1}\leq p_{2},p_{1}=\omega(1/n),p_{1}=o(|\lambda_{1}|),\text{ and }|\lambda_{1}|\geq|\lambda_{2}|. $$

This further implies the following two inequalities:

$$ \displaystyle p_{1}|\lambda_{1}|^{s}\geq p_{2}|\lambda_{2}|^{s}\text{ for any }s\geq t. $$

This is true since $\frac{p_{1}|\lambda_{1}|^{s}}{p_{2}|\lambda_{2}|^{s}}=\frac{p_{1}|\lambda_{1}|^{t}}{p_{2}|\lambda_{2}|^{t}}\times\Big(\frac{|\lambda_{1}|}{|\lambda_{2}|}\Big)^{s-t},$ which is a product of terms at least equal to 1.

$$ \displaystyle|(p_{1}\lambda_{1}^{s}+p_{2}\lambda_{2}^{s})|^{\frac{1}{s+1}}\gtrsim_{D}|(p_{1}\lambda_{1}^{t}+p_{2}\lambda_{2}^{t})|^{\frac{1}{t+1}}\text{ for any even $s\in[t,D].$} $$

Indeed, from (51), it is enough to show that

$$ (p_{1}|\lambda_{1}|^{s})^{\frac{1}{s+1}}\geq(p_{1}|\lambda_{1}|^{t})^{\frac{1}{t+1}}\Longleftrightarrow|\lambda_{1}|^{s-t}\geq p_{1}^{s-t} $$

which follows from $s\geq t,p_{1}=o(|\lambda_{1}|).$

Furthermore, (48) implies that

$$ \displaystyle|\lambda_{1}|=\omega\Big((p_{1}|\lambda_{1}|^{t})^{/t+1}\Big)=\omega\Big(|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{t})|^{1/(t+1)})=\omega(n^{-1/2}). $$

Finally, from (52), we assume that $t=D.$

#### Step 2: Analysis of Variance of SBM.

We need to show that

$$ \Big|\E_{\mathbf{G}\sim\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}\big[\mathsf{SC}_{\mathsf{Star}_{D}}(\mathbf{G})\big]\Big|=\omega\Big(\var_{\mathbf{G}\sim\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}\big[\mathsf{SC}_{\mathsf{Star}_{D}}(\mathbf{G})]^{1/2}\Big). $$

As in the proof of Theorem 2.4, take any graph $H$ which is isomorphic to $S_{1}\otimes S_{2}$ where $S_{1},S_{2}$ are both isomorphic to $\mathsf{Star}_{D}$ and share at least one vertex. Suppose that there are $M_{H}$ copies of the signed count of $H$ after expanding $\var_{\mathbf{G}\sim\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}\big[\mathsf{SC}_{\mathsf{Star}_{D}}(\mathbf{G})].$ Then, we have to show that

$$ n^{2(D+1)}(p_{1}\lambda_{1}^{D}+p_{2}\lambda_{2}^{D})^{2}=\omega\Big(M_{H}\times\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(H)\Big). $$

We consider three possible cases for $H=S_{1}\otimes S_{2}:$

#### Case 1) $S_{1}$ and $S_{2}$ share their central vertex.

Then, $H$ is a star on $\ell\leq 2D$ leaves. This means that $S_{1}$ and $S_{2}$ also share $(2D-\ell)/2$ leaves. Altogether, $|\mathsf{V}(S_{1})\cup\mathsf{V}(S_{2})|=1+\ell+(2D-\ell)/2=1+D+\ell/2.$ Hence, $M_{H}=\Theta(n^{1+D+\ell/2}).$ All we need to prove is that

$$ \begin{split}&n^{2(D+1)}(p_{1}\lambda_{1}^{D}+p_{2}\lambda_{2}^{D})^{2}=\omega(n^{1+D+\ell/2}(p_{1}\lambda_{1}^{\ell}+p_{2}\lambda_{2}^{\ell}))\Longleftrightarrow\\
&n^{1+D-\ell/2}\max(p^{2}_{1}\lambda_{1}^{2D},p^{2}_{2}\lambda_{2}^{2D})=\omega(p_{1}\lambda_{1}^{\ell}+p_{2}\lambda_{2}^{\ell}).\end{split} $$

Again, there are two cases. If $\ell\geq D,$ then by (51) the inequality is equivalent to

$$ n^{1+D-\ell/2}p^{2}_{1}\lambda_{1}^{2D}=\omega(p_{1}\lambda_{1}^{\ell})\Longleftrightarrow n^{1+D-\ell/2}p_{1}\lambda_{1}^{2D-\ell}=\omega(1). $$

Note that $p_{1}=\omega(1/n)$ and $|\lambda_{1}|=\omega(n^{-1/2})$ by (53), which is enough.

If $\ell<D,$ then $|p_{1}\lambda_{1}^{\ell}+p_{2}\lambda_{2}^{\ell}|=|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{\ell})|\lesssim_{D}|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{D})|^{\frac{\ell+1}{D+1}},$ so the inequality reduces to

$$ n^{1+D-\ell/2}|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{D})|^{2-\frac{\ell+1}{D+1}}=\omega(1), $$

which follows immediately from (48).

#### Case 2) $S_{1}$ and $S_{2}$ do not have a common central vertex and do not have common edges.

Hence, $S_{1}\otimes S_{2}$ has at most $2(D+1)-1$ vertices (at $S_{1},S_{2}$ need to share at least one vertex) and $2D$ edges. Hence, $M_{H}=O(n^{2D+1}).$ By Theorem 3.6 applied for $2D,$ $|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(S_{1}\otimes S_{2})|\lesssim_{D}|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{2D})|.$ Hence, all we need to show is that

$$ n^{2(D+1)}(p_{1}\lambda_{1}^{D}+p_{2}\lambda_{2}^{D})^{2}=\omega(n^{1+2D}(p_{1}\lambda_{1}^{2D}+p_{2}\lambda_{2}^{2D}). $$

This is a special case of (54) proved in Case 1) when $\ell=2D.$

#### Case 3) $S_{1}$ and $S_{2}$ do not have a common central vertex but do have common edges.

Note that $S_{1},S_{2}$ are stars and do not share their central vertex, they can have at most one common edge. Hence, $S_{1}\otimes S_{2}$ has at most $2D-2$ edges, so $|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(S_{1}\otimes S_{2})|\lesssim_{D}|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{2D-2})|$ by Theorem 3.6 applied for $2D.$ As $S_{1},S_{2}$ share an edge, they have at least two common vertices, so $|\mathsf{V}(S_{1})\cup\mathsf{V}(S_{2})|\leq 2(D+1)-2\leq 2D.$ Thus, $M_{H}=O(n^{2D}).$ Altogether, we need to prove that

$$ n^{2(D+1)}(p_{1}\lambda_{1}^{D}+p_{2}\lambda_{2}^{D})^{2}=\omega(n^{2D}(p_{1}\lambda_{1}^{2D-2}+p_{2}\lambda_{2}^{2D-2}). $$

This is a special case of (54) proved in Case 1) when $\ell=2D-2.$ ∎

## 4 Comparison Inequalities

We note that all arguments in the current section apply more generally to any graphon instead of stochastic block model, provided no measurability issues occur.

### 4.1 Cycle Comparisons: A Spectral Approach

We prove the following theorem, which explains why signed triangles and 4-cycles are used for detecting stochastic block models, but larger cycles are not.

#### Theorem 4.1.

For any $\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)$ distribution and $t\geq 5,$

$$ \Psi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{t})\leq\Psi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4}). $$

#### Proof.

Consider the expression for a signed $t$ -cycle count. It is given by

$$ \begin{split}\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{t})&=\sum_{x_{1},x_{2},\ldots,x_{t}}p_{x_{1}}p_{x_{2}}\cdots p_{x_{t}}Q_{x_{1}x_{2}}Q_{x_{2}x_{3}}\cdots Q_{x_{t}x_{1}}\\
&=\sum_{x_{1},x_{2},\ldots,x_{t}}(\sqrt{p_{x_{1}}}Q_{x_{1},x_{2}}\sqrt{p_{x_{2}}})(\sqrt{p_{x_{2}}}Q_{x_{2},x_{3}}\sqrt{p_{x_{3}}})\cdots(\sqrt{p_{x_{t}}}Q_{x_{t},x_{1}}\sqrt{p_{x_{1}}})\\
&=\mathsf{tr}((\sqrt{P}Q\sqrt{P})^{t}),\end{split} $$

where $\sqrt{P}$ is the diagonal matrix with entries $(\sqrt{p_{1}},\sqrt{p_{2}},\ldots,\sqrt{p_{k}}).$ Let $\lambda_{1},\lambda_{2},\ldots,\lambda_{k}$ be the k eigenvalues of $\sqrt{P}Q\sqrt{P}.$ Then,

$$ \Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{t})=\sum_{i=1}^{k}\lambda_{i}^{t}. $$

Now, for any $t\geq 5,$

$$ |\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{t})|^{1/t}=\Big|\sum_{i=1}^{k}\lambda_{i}^{t}\Big|^{1/t}\leq(\sum_{i=1}^{k}|\lambda_{i}|^{t})^{1/t}\leq(\sum_{i=1}^{k}|\lambda_{i}|^{4})^{1/4}=|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4})|^{1/4}. $$

The first inequality is triangle inequality and the second monotonicity of $t\longrightarrow\|(\lambda_{1},\ldots,\lambda_{k})\|_{t}.$ ∎

#### Remark 2 (Triangles vs 4-Cycles).

The above proof also sheds light on when triangles are more informative than 4-cycles and vice versa. Namely, observe that if the positive (or negative) eigenvalues of $\sqrt{P}Q\sqrt{P}$ dominate, then

$$ \Big|\sum_{i=1}^{k}\lambda_{i}^{3}\Big|^{1/3}\approx\Big|\sum_{i=1}^{k}|\lambda_{i}|^{3}\Big|^{1/3}\geq\Big|\sum_{i=1}^{k}\lambda_{i}^{4}\Big|^{1/4}, $$

so $|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{3})|^{1/3}\geq c|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4})|^{1/4}.$ Whenever this is not the case (as in the quiet planted coloring distribution in [KVWX23], the $L_{\infty}$ random geometric graphs in [BB24a], certain non-PSD Gaussian random geometric graphs in [BB25]), the mass on positive and negative eigenvalues should be relatively balanced. Heuristically, this is caused by certain bipartiteness/hyperbolic behavior of $\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q).$

A more detailed analysis of the performance of signed triangles and 4-cycles for testing against sparser Erdős-Rényi as well is carried out in [JKL19].

### 4.2 Exploiting Symmetries: A Sum-of-Squares Approach

We prove the following theorem, which explains why signed $\mathsf{K}_{4}^{-}$ counts are not used for detecting latent space structure, where $\mathsf{K}_{4}^{-}$ is the graph on 4 vertices and 5 edges (say with vertex set $\{1,2,3,4\}$ and all edges but $(2,4)$ ). One can certainly generalize this approach to other graphs with enough symmetry. The argument appears implicitly in [LR23a, Lemma 4.10].

#### Theorem 4.2.

For any $\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)$ distribution,

$$ |\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(K_{4}^{-})|\leq|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4})|. $$

#### Proof.

Consider the $\mathsf{Cyc}_{4}$ with edges $(12),(23),(34),(14)$ and the $K_{4}^{-}$ on these edges with the extra edge $(13).$ We will first rewrite the expression for $\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4}).$ Note that

$$ \begin{split}\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4})&=\E_{\mathbf{x}_{1},\mathbf{x}_{2},\mathbf{x}_{3},\mathbf{x}_{4}}[Q_{\mathbf{x}_{1},\mathbf{x}_{2}}Q_{\mathbf{x}_{2},\mathbf{x}_{3}}Q_{\mathbf{x}_{3},\mathbf{x}_{4}}Q_{\mathbf{x}_{4},\mathbf{x}_{1}}]\\
&=\E_{\mathbf{x}_{1},\mathbf{x}_{3}}\Big[\E_{\mathbf{x}_{2},\mathbf{x}_{4}}[Q_{\mathbf{x}_{1},\mathbf{x}_{2}}Q_{\mathbf{x}_{2},\mathbf{x}_{3}}Q_{\mathbf{x}_{3},\mathbf{x}_{4}}Q_{\mathbf{x}_{4},\mathbf{x}_{1}}|\mathbf{x}_{1},\mathbf{x}_{3}]\Big].\end{split} $$

Note that $\mathbf{x}_{2},\mathbf{x}_{4}$ are independent even conditioned on $\mathbf{x}_{1},\mathbf{x}_{3}.$ Hence,

$$ \displaystyle\E[Q_{\mathbf{x}_{1},\mathbf{x}_{2}}Q_{\mathbf{x}_{2},\mathbf{x}_{3}}Q_{\mathbf{x}_{3},\mathbf{x}_{4}}Q_{\mathbf{x}_{4},\mathbf{x}_{1}}|\mathbf{x}_{1},\mathbf{x}_{3}] \displaystyle=\E[Q_{\mathbf{x}_{1},\mathbf{x}_{2}}Q_{\mathbf{x}_{2},\mathbf{x}_{3}}|\mathbf{x}_{1},\mathbf{x}_{3}]\times\E[Q_{\mathbf{x}_{1},\mathbf{x}_{4}}Q_{\mathbf{x}_{4},\mathbf{x}_{3}}|\mathbf{x}_{1},\mathbf{x}_{3}] \displaystyle=\E[Q_{\mathbf{x}_{1},\mathbf{x}_{2}}Q_{\mathbf{x}_{2},\mathbf{x}_{3}}|\mathbf{x}_{1},\mathbf{x}_{3}]^{2}, $$

where we used the fact that the conditional expectation are identically distributed. Hence, we obtain that

$$ \Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4})=\E\Bigg[\E[Q_{\mathbf{x}_{1},\mathbf{x}_{2}}Q_{\mathbf{x}_{2},\mathbf{x}_{3}}|\mathbf{x}_{1},\mathbf{x}_{3}]^{2}\Bigg]. $$

In the exact same way, we conclude that

$$ \Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(K^{-}_{4})=\E\Bigg[\E[Q_{\mathbf{x}_{1},\mathbf{x}_{2}}Q_{\mathbf{x}_{2},\mathbf{x}_{3}}|\mathbf{x}_{1},\mathbf{x}_{3}]^{2}Q_{\mathbf{x}_{1},\mathbf{x}_{3}}\Bigg]. $$

Altogether,

$$ \displaystyle\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4})-\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(K^{-}_{4})=\E\Bigg[\E[Q_{\mathbf{x}_{1},\mathbf{x}_{2}}Q_{\mathbf{x}_{2},\mathbf{x}_{3}}|\mathbf{x}_{1},\mathbf{x}_{3}]^{2}(1-Q_{\mathbf{x}_{1},\mathbf{x}_{3}})\Bigg]\geq 0, \displaystyle\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4})+\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(K^{-}_{4})=\E\Bigg[\E[Q_{\mathbf{x}_{1},\mathbf{x}_{2}}Q_{\mathbf{x}_{2},\mathbf{x}_{3}}|\mathbf{x}_{1},\mathbf{x}_{3}]^{2}(1+Q_{\mathbf{x}_{1},\mathbf{x}_{3}})\Bigg]\geq 0, $$

where we used that $-1\leq Q_{\mathbf{x}_{1},\mathbf{x}_{3}}\leq 1.$ Together, the two inequalities give the desired result. ∎

### 4.3 Ghost Vertices: A Second Moment Approach

The key idea in the proof of Theorem 4.2 was the symmetry around $(1,3).$ One can “artificially” create such symmetry via a second moment argument, but this unfortunately yields comparison inequalities too weak for the purposes of (5). Here, we present one possible result. The proof follows implicitly [CGW88, Fact 12] and [LR23a, (4) in Section 3].

#### Theorem 4.3.

Consider any graph $H$ and suppose that it has a vertex of degree $d.$ Then, for any $\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)$ distribution,

$$ |\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(H)|\leq|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{K}_{2,d})|^{1/2}. $$

#### Proof.

Let the vertex set of $H$ be $\{1,2,\ldots,h\}$ such that $h$ has degree $d.$ Then,

$$ \begin{split}&|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(H)|=\Bigg|\E\Bigg[\prod_{(i,j)\in\mathsf{E}(H)}Q_{\mathbf{x}_{i}\mathbf{x}_{j}}\Bigg]\Bigg|\\
&=\Bigg|\E\Bigg[\prod_{i,j<h\;:\;(i,j)\in\mathsf{E}(H)}Q_{\mathbf{x}_{i},\mathbf{x}_{j}}\times\E\Big[\prod_{k\;:\;(k,h)\in\mathsf{E}(H)}Q_{\mathbf{x}_{k}\mathbf{x}_{h}}\Big|x_{1},x_{2},\ldots,x_{h-1}\Big]\Bigg]\Bigg|\\
&\leq\E\Bigg[\Bigg|\prod_{i,j<h\;:\;(i,j)\in\mathsf{E}(H)}Q_{\mathbf{x}_{i},\mathbf{x}_{j}}\times\E\Big[\prod_{k\;:\;(k,h)\in\mathsf{E}(H)}Q_{\mathbf{x}_{k}\mathbf{x}_{h}}\Big|x_{1},x_{2},\ldots,x_{h-1}\Big]\Bigg|\Bigg]\\
&\leq\E\Bigg[\Bigg|\E\Big[\prod_{k\;:\;(k,h)\in\mathsf{E}(H)}Q_{\mathbf{x}_{k}\mathbf{x}_{h}}\Big|x_{1},x_{2},\ldots,x_{h-1}\Big]\Bigg|\Bigg]\\
&\leq\E\Bigg[\E\Big[\prod_{k\;:\;(k,h)\in\mathsf{E}(H)}Q_{\mathbf{x}_{k}\mathbf{x}_{h}}\Big|x_{1},x_{2},\ldots,x_{h-1}\Big]^{2}\Bigg]^{1/2}\\
&=\E_{\mathbf{x}_{1},\mathbf{x}_{2},\ldots,\mathbf{x}_{h-1},\mathbf{x}_{h^{\prime}},\mathbf{x}_{h^{\prime\prime}}}\Bigg[\prod_{k\;:\;(k,h)\in\mathsf{E}(H)}Q_{\mathbf{x}_{k}\mathbf{x}_{h^{\prime}}}Q_{\mathbf{x}_{k}\mathbf{x}_{h^{\prime\prime}}}\Bigg]^{1/2}=|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{K}_{2,d})|^{1/2}.\qed\end{split} $$

## 5 Future Directions

Beyond the natural direction of proving Conjecture 1 for all stochastic block models (and, more generally, graphons), we outline several different directions of interest. They modify the conditions in the current work in different ways.

#### 1. Beyond dense graphs: testing against a sparse Erdős-Rényi.

One natural direction is to develop a quasirandomness theory for testing against ${\mathbb{G}(n,q)}$ when $q$ depends on $n,$ say $q=n^{-\beta}$ for some absolute constant $\beta\in(0,1].$ The $q$ -biased Fourier coefficients are

$$ \Phi^{q}_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(H)\coloneqq\E\Bigg[\prod_{(i,j)\in\mathsf{E}(H)}\frac{(\mathbf{G}_{ij}-q)}{\sqrt{q(1-q)}}\Bigg]\asymp n^{\frac{\beta\times|\mathsf{E}(H)|}{2}}\times\E\Bigg[\prod_{(i,j)\in\mathsf{E}(H)}{(\mathbf{G}_{ij}-q)}\Bigg], $$

where the asymptotic equivalence holds for constant sized graphs $H.$ The equivalent condition to (5) is $|\Phi^{q}_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(H)|^{\frac{1}{|\mathsf{V}(H)|}}=\omega(n^{-1/2}).$ What makes this problem different is the $n^{\frac{\beta\times|\mathsf{E}(H)|}{2|\mathsf{V}(H)|}}$ term in $|\Phi^{q}_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(H)|^{\frac{1}{|\mathsf{V}(H)|}}.$ This term poses several challenges, including the argument on the variance of the planted model in Theorem 2.4. One viable approach seems the consideration of balanced graphs which [DMW25] use exactly in the setting of planting a dense subgraph in ${\mathbb{G}(n,q)}.$ In a balanced graph $H,$ the key quantity $\frac{|\mathsf{E}(H)|}{|\mathsf{V}(H)|}$ is larger than the same quantity for any subgraph $H^{\prime}$ of $H.$

#### 2. Beyond SBMs: testing against vertex-transitive distributions.

The question of developing quasirandomness theory for testing against ${\mathbb{G}(n,1/2)}$ is, of course, not restricted to stochastic block models as in our work and planted subgraph models as in [YZZ24]. In fact, one can even ask the question for fixed graphs as in the original quasrirandomness work of [CGW88].

One way to phrase Problem 1 for a fixed graph is as follows. Take any fixed graph $G$ and let $\Pi_{G}$ be the distribution formed by applying a uniformly random vertex permutation to $G.$ Find the possible approximate maximizers of $H\longrightarrow\Psi_{\Pi_{G}}(H)$ where $H$ ranges over constant-sized graphs without isolated vertices.

#### 3. Beyond constant degree tests: towards computational hardness.

Our results as well as the results of [YZZ24] apply only to indistinguishability against constant-degree polynomial tests. However, it would be useful to have results for polynomials of higher-degree. Especially desirable would be hardness against degree $D=\omega(\log n)$ polynomial tests as this is frequently viewed as strong (even though by no means perfect) evidence for computational hardness.

Our current framework does not allow for any super-constant $D$ since one can check that the implicit constants in $\gtrsim_{D}$ are on the order of $2^{\Theta(D\log D)}$ (when enumerating over all graphs on at most $D$ edges in Theorem 2.3 and taking max over $K$ in Theorems 3.3 and 3.6). Explicitly, this means that when $D=\omega(1),$ the different $\gtrsim_{D}$ factors no longer indicate inequalities up to absolute constants. Yet, if we allow for an $n^{o(1)}$ blow-up in the sample complexity, the same techniques with a more careful bookkeeping of the $\gtrsim_{D}$ dependence still apply. To illustrate, useful is the following sample-complexity formulation of (HT).

#### Definition 3 (“Vertex”-Sample-Complexity Perspective of Testing against Erdős-Rényi).

Consider a sequence of stochastic block-models $\bigg\{\mathbb{SBM}(p^{k},Q^{k})\bigg\}_{k\in\mathbb{N}}$ such that each coordinate of $p^{k}$ is positive and $Q^{k}$ is not the zero matrix. Find the minimal number of vertices $n(k)$ such that one can test between $\mathbb{SBM}(n(k);p^{k},Q^{k})$ and $\mathbb{G}(n(k),1/2)$ via a degree- $D$ polynomial test with success probability $1-o_{k}(1).$

With a small blow-up in the sample-complexity, we can show the following theorem. The proofs are identical, observing that the hidden factors are on the order of $2^{O(D\log D)}$ everywhere. Hence, if $D=o(\log n/\log\log n),$ the hidden factors are of order $n^{o(1)}.$

#### Proposition 5.1.

Suppose that there is a degree $D=o(\log n/\log\log n)$ polynomial test that succeeds in distinguishing $\mathbb{SBM}(n(k);p^{k},Q^{k})$ and $\mathbb{G}(n(k),1/2)$ with success probability $1-o_{k}(1).$ Suppose furthermore that the family $\mathbb{SBM}(n(k);p^{k},Q^{k})$ belongs to one of the four cases $i\in\{1,2,3,4\}$ described in Theorem 1.4. Then, for some appropriate $\epsilon_{k}=o_{k}(1),$ there exists some signed subgraph count of $H\in\mathcal{A}^{i}_{D}$ that distinguishes $\mathbb{SBM}(n(k)^{1+\epsilon_{k}};p^{k},Q^{k})$ and $\mathbb{G}(n(k)^{1+\epsilon_{k}},1/2)$ with success probability $1-o_{k}(1).$

The reason why we write all the proofs for constant degree instead of $o(\log n/\log\log n)$ is that while we are not aware of any advantage of the $o(\log n/\log\log n)$ tests, there is significant notational simplicity when hiding factors depending on the degree. Of course, if one manages to push the result to degree $\Theta(\log n),$ this would have the significant advantage of capturing spectral methods. However, this seems to be not merely a matter of carefully keeping track of the constants in our proofs. If any form of Conjecture 1 holds true for degree $D=\omega(\log n)$ polynomial tests, it seems to require essentially new techniques.

#### Remark 3 (Completeness of Definition 3).

A-priori, it is not even clear that $n(k)$ in Definition 3 exists. Yet, a simple argument mimicking Claim 3.4 and Lemma 3.2 shows that

$$ \Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4})=\Omega\Big(\max_{i,j}p_{i}^{2}p_{j}^{2}|Q_{i,j}|^{4}\Big) $$

for any $\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q).$ As the variance under planted scales as $O_{k}(n^{7})=o_{k}(n^{2|\mathsf{V}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4})|}),$ one can use this to show that for large enough $n(k),$ one can always test via the signed 4-cycle count.

#### 4. Beyond complete graphs: “edge”-sample-complexity of testing.

A different sample complexity perspective of graph hypothesis testing was introduced in [MVW24] and further analyzed in [BB24b]. The goal is to capture the query-complexity of low-degree polynomial tests. We take the following formulation as described in [BB24b].

For a mask $\mathcal{M}\in\{\textsf{view, hide}\}^{N\times N}$ and (adjacency) matrix $A\in\{0,1\}^{N\times N},$ denote by $A\odot\mathcal{M}$ the $N\times N$ array in which $(A\odot\mathcal{M})_{ji}=A_{ji}$ whenever $\mathcal{M}_{ji}=\textsf{view}$ and $(A\odot\mathcal{M})_{ji}=\,\,?$ whenever $\mathcal{M}_{ji}=\textsf{hide}.$ Testing between graph distributions with masks corresponds to a non-adaptive edge query model. Instead of viewing a full graph, one can choose to observe a smaller more structured set $\mathcal{M}$ of edges in order to obtain a more data-efficient algorithm. The number of view entries $|\mathcal{M}|$ of $\mathcal{M}$ is a natural proxy for “sample complexity” in the case of low-degree polynomials as the input variables of low-degree polynomials are edges rather than vertices. Instead of asking for $n(k)$ in Definition 3, one can ask for the size of the optimal mask $\mathcal{M}(k).$

#### Definition 4 (“Edge”-Sample-Complexity Perspective of Testing against Erdős-Rényi).

Consider a sequence of stochastic block-models $\bigg\{\mathbb{SBM}(p^{k},Q^{k})\bigg\}_{k\in\mathbb{N}}$ such that each coordinate of $p^{k}$ is positive and $Q^{k}$ is not the zero matrix. Find the minimal number of edges $M_{k}$ such that there exists some $N(k)\in\mathbb{N}$ and a mask $\mathcal{M}_{k}$ of size $|\mathcal{M}_{k}|=M_{k}$ on $N(k)$ vertices with the following property. One can test between $\mathcal{M}_{k}\odot\mathbb{SBM}(N(k);p^{k},Q^{k})$ and $\mathcal{M}_{k}\odot\mathbb{G}(N(k),1/2)$ via a degree- $D$ polynomial test with success probability $1-o_{k}(1).$

Again, one can ask for a quasirandomness criterion in the case of edge-query-complexity. A theorem due to Alon [Alo81] shows that the maximal number of graphs isomorphic to $H$ in a graph on $M$ edges is $\Theta_{H}(M^{\frac{|\mathsf{V}(H)|+\delta(H)}{2}}),$ where

$$ \delta(H)\coloneqq\max_{S\subseteq\mathsf{V}(H)}|S|-|\{j\in\mathsf{V}(H)\;:\;\exists i\in S\text{ s.t. }(j,i)\in\mathsf{E}(H)\}|. $$

Reasoning as in Section 1.3, instead of finding the approximate maximizers of $H\longrightarrow|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(H)|^{\frac{1}{|\mathsf{V}(H)|}},$ one should look for the approximate maximizers of

$$ H\longrightarrow|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(H)|^{\frac{1}{|\mathsf{V}(H)|+\delta(H)}}. $$

Needless to say, different techniques than ours are required.

#### 5. The Sign of Fourier Coefficients of Stochastic Block Models.

The argument of Lemma 3.2 shows that for any $\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)$ such that $Q$ is not the zero matrix, $\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4})>0.$ What other graphs $H$ besides $\mathsf{Cyc}_{4}$ have this property? The argument in Lemma 3.2 applies verbatim for any other graph $\mathsf{K}_{2,d}$ when $d$ is even. The examples in Appendix A show that $H$ does not necessarily satisfy this property if $H$ has an odd degree vertex (Theorem A.2), $H$ has an odd number of edges (Theorem A.6), $H$ is not 2-connected (Theorem A.7), or $H$ is not bipartite (Theorem A.5).

What if we relax the inequality: what graphs $H$ have the property that $\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(H)\geq 0$ for any $\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)$ ? The argument in Theorem 4.1 shows that all cycles of even length, in addition to the graphs $\mathsf{K}_{2,d}$ satisfy this property.
