## Appendix A Library of Examples

We will repeatedly refer to the following condition.

#### Proposition A.1.

We call an $\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)$ distribution on $k$ communities fully unbiased if for any $x\in[k],$ it holds that $\sum_{y}p_{y}Q_{x,y}=0.$ For any fully unbiased $\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)$ and graph $H$ with a leaf (in particular, any tree), $\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(H)=0.$

#### Proof.

Suppose that $H$ has $h$ vertices and vertex $h$ is a leaf with parent $h-1.$ By Proposition 1.3,

$$ \displaystyle\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(H)=\sum_{x_{1},x_{2},\ldots,x_{h}\in[k]}\Bigg(\prod_{i=1}^{h}p_{x_{i}}\times\prod_{(i,j)\in\mathsf{E}(H)}Q_{x_{i},x_{j}}\Bigg) \displaystyle=\sum_{x_{1},x_{2},\ldots,x_{h-1}\in[k]}\Bigg(\prod_{i=1}^{h-1}p_{x_{i}}\times\prod_{(i,j)\in\mathsf{E}(H)\backslash\{(h-1,h)\}}Q_{x_{i},x_{j}}\times\sum_{x_{h}\in[k]}Q_{x_{h-1},x_{h}}\Bigg)=0, $$

where we use the fully unbiased condition for $x=x_{h-1}.$ ∎

Throughout, we only verify condition (5), but do not compute the variance of the planted model.

#### Theorem A.2 (Failure of All Signed Trees).

There exists an SBM distribution $\mathbb{SBM}(n;p,Q)$ on $k=2$ communities with $p=(1/2,1/2)$ which has the following properties. For any graph $H$ with an odd degree vertex, $\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(H)=0.$ For any graph $H$ without odd degree vertices, $\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(H)=1.$ Furthermore, as $n$ grows, $\mathbb{SBM}(n;p,Q)$ can be distinguished from ${\mathbb{G}(n,1/2)}$ with high probability via the signed 4-cycle count, for example. Finally, any signed subgraph count distinguishes $\mathbb{SBM}(n;p,|Q|)$ and ${\mathbb{G}(n,1/2)}$ with high probability as $n$ grows.

#### Construction.

Take $k=2,p=(1/2,1/2)$ and $Q=\begin{pmatrix}1&-1\\ -1&1\end{pmatrix}.$ ∎

#### Theorem A.3 (Balanced 2-SBMs in which 1-Stars Dominate).

There exists a stochastic block model $\mathbb{SBM}(n;p,Q)$ on 2 balanced communities with the following property. It can be distinguished from ${\mathbb{G}(n,1/2)}$ with high probability via the signed count of 1-stars, but not via the signed counts of any other connected graph of constant size.

#### Construction.

Consider the following SBM model on $k=2$ communities. $p=(1/2,1/2)$ and $Q=\begin{pmatrix}n^{-\beta}&0\\ 0&n^{-\beta}\end{pmatrix}$ where $\beta\in(3/4,1).$ For any connected graph $H,$ $\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(n;p,Q)}(H)=O(n^{-\beta|\mathsf{E}(H)|}).$ Hence, if $H$ has at least 2 edges and is connected, $\Psi_{\mathbb{SBM}(n;p,Q)}(H)=O(n^{-\beta\frac{|\mathsf{E}(H)|}{|\mathsf{V}(H)|}})=O(n^{-2\beta/3})=o(n^{-1/2})$ as $\beta\geq 3/4.$ Then, $\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(n;p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{1})=\Theta(n^{-\beta})$ and $\Psi_{\mathbb{SBM}(n;p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{1})=\Theta(n^{-\beta/3})=\omega(n^{-1/2})$ as $\beta\leq 1.$ ∎

#### Theorem A.4 (Balanced 2-SBMs in which 2-Stars Dominate).

There exists a stochastic block model $\mathbb{SBM}(n;p,Q)$ on 2 balanced communities with the following property. It can be distinguished from ${\mathbb{G}(n,1/2)}$ with high probability via the signed count of 2-stars, but not via the signed counts of any other connected graph of constant size.

#### Construction.

Consider the following SBM model on $k=2$ communities. $p=(1/2,1/2)$ and $Q=\begin{pmatrix}n^{-\beta}&0\\ 0&-n^{-\beta}\end{pmatrix}$ where $\beta\in(2/3,3/4).$ For any connected graph $H,$ $\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(n;p,Q)}(H)=O(n^{-\beta|\mathsf{E}(H)|}).$ Hence, if $H$ has at least 3 edges and is connected, $\Psi_{\mathbb{SBM}(n;p,Q)}(H)=O(n^{-\beta\frac{|\mathsf{E}(H)|}{|\mathsf{V}(H)|}})=O(n^{-3\beta/4})=o(n^{-1/2})$ as $\beta\geq 2/3.$ Then, $\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(n;p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{2})=\Theta(n^{-2\beta})$ and $\Psi_{\mathbb{SBM}(n;p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{2})=\Theta(n^{-2\beta/3})=\omega(n^{-1/2})$ as $\beta\leq 3/4.$ Finally, $\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(n;p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{1})=0.$ ∎

#### Theorem A.5 (2-SBMs in which Large Stars Dominate).

Let $D\geq 3$ be a natural number. There exists a stochastic block model $\mathbb{SBM}(n;p,Q)$ on 2 communities with the following property. It can be distinguished from ${\mathbb{G}(n,1/2)}$ with high probability via the signed count of $D$ -stars, but not via the signed count of any other connected graph on at most $D$ edges.

#### Construction.

Consider the following SBM model on $k=2$ communities. $p=(n^{-\alpha},1-n^{-\alpha})$ and $Q=\begin{pmatrix}0&n^{-\beta}\\ n^{-\beta}&0\end{pmatrix}$ where $\alpha=3/4,\beta=\frac{2D-1}{4D}-\frac{1}{8D(D-1)}.$ Let $H$ be any connected graph. If $H$ is not bipartite, clearly $\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(H)=0.$ Now, suppose that $H$ is bipartite and has parts of sizes $u$ and $v$ where $1\leq u\leq v$ and $u+v=|\mathsf{V}(H)|\leq D+1.$ A simple calculation shows that

$$ \Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(H)=\Theta(p_{1}^{u}n^{-\beta|\mathsf{E}(H)|})=\Theta(n^{-\alpha u-\beta|\mathsf{E}(H)|})\Longrightarrow\Psi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(H)=\Theta(n^{-\alpha\frac{u}{|\mathsf{V}(H)|}-\beta\frac{|\mathsf{E}(H)|}{|\mathsf{V}(H)|}}). $$

Now, suppose first that $H$ is not a tree. A non-tree bipartite graph on at most $D$ edges has at most $D$ vertices and each part in the bipartition is of size at least 2. Thus,

$$ \Psi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(H)=O(n^{-\frac{3}{2D}-\frac{2D-1}{4D}+\frac{1}{8D(D-1)}})O(n^{-\frac{1}{2}-\frac{10D-11}{8D(D-1)}})=o(n^{-1/2}). $$

Next, if $H$ is a tree and $u\geq 2,$

$$ \Psi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(H)=O(n^{-\frac{3}{2}\frac{1}{|\mathsf{V}(H)|}-\beta\times\frac{|\mathsf{V}(H)|-1}{|\mathsf{V}(H)|}}). $$

As $\beta<3/2,$ the convex combination $\frac{3}{2}\frac{1}{|\mathsf{V}(H)|}+\beta\times\frac{|\mathsf{V}(H)|-1}{|\mathsf{V}(H)|}$ decreases with $|\mathsf{V}(H)|,$ hence is maximized at $|\mathsf{V}(H)|=D+1,$ where

$$ n^{-\frac{3}{2}\frac{1}{|\mathsf{V}(H)|}-\beta\times\frac{|\mathsf{V}(H)|-1}{|\mathsf{V}(H)|}}=n^{-\frac{3}{2}\times\frac{1}{D+1}-(\frac{2D-1}{4D}-\frac{1}{8D(D-1)})\times\frac{D}{D+1}}=n^{-\frac{1}{2}-\frac{6D-7}{8(D-1)(D+1)}}=o(n^{-1/2}). $$

Finally, if $H$ is a tree and $u=1,$ we obtain

$$ \Psi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(H)=\Theta(n^{-\frac{3}{4}\frac{1}{|\mathsf{V}(H)|}-\beta\times\frac{|\mathsf{V}(H)|-1}{|\mathsf{V}(H)|}}). $$

When $|\mathsf{V}(H)|=D+1,$ the case of $\mathsf{Star}_{D},$

$$ n^{-\frac{3}{4}\frac{1}{|\mathsf{V}(H)|}-\beta\times\frac{|\mathsf{V}(H)|-1}{|\mathsf{V}(H)|}}=n^{-\frac{3}{4}\frac{1}{D+1}-(\frac{2D-1}{4D}-\frac{1}{8D(D-1)})\frac{D}{D+1}}=n^{-\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{8(D-1)(D+1)}}=\omega(n^{-1/2}). $$

When $|\mathsf{V}(H)|<D+1,$ the case of smaller stars,

$$ n^{-\frac{3}{4}\frac{1}{|\mathsf{V}(H)|}-\beta\times\frac{|\mathsf{V}(H)|-1}{|\mathsf{V}(H)|}}\leq n^{-\frac{3}{4}\frac{1}{D}-(\frac{2D-1}{4D}-\frac{1}{8D(D-1)})\frac{D-1}{D}}=n^{-\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{8D^{2}}}=o(n^{-1/2}). $$

Thus, $\mathsf{Star}_{D}$ is the only connected graph on at most $D$ edges such that $\Psi_{\mathbb{SBM}(n;p,Q)}=\omega(n^{-1/2}).$ ∎

#### Theorem A.6 (2-SBMs in which 4-Cycles Dominate).

There exists an SBM distribution $\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)$ with the following properties. All Fourier coefficients corresponding to graphs with at least one leaf (including all stars) are zero and the Fourier coefficients corresponding to graphs with an odd number of edges (including triangles) are zero. Furthermore, the 4-cycle is the unique connected graph of constant size which can distinguish $\mathbb{SBM}(n;p,Q)$ and ${\mathbb{G}(n,1/2)}$ with high probability.

#### Construction.

The construction is inspired by the “quiet planting” distribution in [KVWX23]. Take some $q\in\mathbb{N}$ such that $q=\omega(n^{5/8}),q=o(n^{2/3})$ and consider an SBM on $k=q^{2}$ communities labeled by $[q]\times[q],$ where $p_{(a,b)}=1/q^{2}\quad\forall(a,b)\in[q]\times[q]$ and

$$ \displaystyle Q_{(a_{1},b_{1}),(a_{2},b_{2})}=\begin{cases}1,&a_{1}=b_{1}\text{ and }a_{2}\neq b_{2},\\
-1,&a_{1}\neq b_{1}\text{ and }a_{2}=b_{2},\\
\ 0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases} $$

The Fourier coefficient corresponding to any graph with a leaf (including stars) is 0 as the SBM is fully unbiased as in Proposition A.1.

The Fourier coefficient corresponding to any graph with an odd number of edges (including triangles) is also 0. This follows since the measure-preserving map on labels $(a,b)\longrightarrow(b,a)$ acts by $Q_{b,a}=-Q_{a,b}.$ This is enough via (7).

Finally, the Fourier coefficient of any connected graph $H$ is $O(q^{1-|\mathsf{V}(H)|})$ and the Fourier coefficient of the signed 4-cycle is $\Theta(q^{-3}).$ In particular, this means that if $H$ is connected, $\Psi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(H)=O(q^{-\frac{|\mathsf{V}(H)|-1}{|\mathsf{V}(H)|}}).$ As $q=\omega(n^{5/8}),$ this means that $\Psi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(H)=o(n^{-1/2})$ if $|\mathsf{V}(H)|\geq 5.$ On the other hand, $\Psi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4})=\Theta(q^{-3/4})=\omega(n^{-1/2})$ as $q=o(n^{2/3}).$ Finally, any other connected graph $H$ on at most 4 vertices has either an odd number of edges or an odd degree vertex, so $\Psi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(H)=0.$ ∎

#### Theorem A.7 (2-SBMs in which Triangles Dominate).

There exists a stochastic block model $\mathbb{SBM}(n;p,Q)$ which can be distinguished from ${\mathbb{G}(n,1/2)}$ with high probability via the signed triangle count, but not via the signed count of any other connected graph on a constant number of vertices.

#### Construction.

One such construction appears in [KVWX23] and with a slight modification in [BB24b]. We give full detail for completeness. Take $k=n^{\alpha}$ for some $\alpha\in(2/3,3/4).$ Consider an SBM on $k$ communities with $p_{i}=1/k=n^{-\alpha}\quad\forall i\in[k]$ and

$$ Q_{i,j}=\begin{cases}1,&i=j,\\
-\frac{1}{k-1},&i\neq j.\end{cases} $$

Let $H$ be any connected graph. One can again observe that the SBM is fully unbiased, which implies that $\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(H)=0$ if $H$ is a tree via Proposition A.1. Similarly, one can show that if $H$ has any edge the removal of which makes the graph disconnected (i.e., $H$ is not 2-connected), $\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(H)=0.$

Finally, if $H$ is 2-connected, that is $H$ is connected and continues to be so after the removal of any edge, one can show that $\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(H)\asymp k^{1-|\mathsf{V}(H)|}.$ Hence, $\Psi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q)}(H)\asymp k^{-\frac{|\mathsf{V}(H)|-1}{|\mathsf{V}(H)|}}.$ This quantity is decreasing in $|\mathsf{V}(H)|.$ As $k=o(n^{3/4})$ and $k=\omega(n^{2/3}),$ the signed triangle count is the unique signed count of a connected constant-sized graph sufficient for testing. ∎

#### Theorem A.8 (One-to-One Comparisons of Fourier Coefficients Fail).

There exist two stochastic block models $\mathbb{SBM}(n;p^{1},Q^{1})$ and $\mathbb{SBM}(n;p^{2},Q^{2})$ on 2 communities and a connected graph $H$ on $6$ vertices and 8 edges with the following two properties:

- 1. In $\mathbb{SBM}(n;p^{1},Q^{1}),$ $\Psi_{\mathbb{SBM}(n;p^{1},Q^{1})}(\mathsf{Star}_{t})=o(\Psi_{\mathbb{SBM}(n;p^{1},Q^{1})}(H))$ for any $t\in\mathbb{N}.$

- 2. In $\mathbb{SBM}(n;p^{2},Q^{2}),$ $\Psi_{\mathbb{SBM}(n;p^{2},Q^{2})}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4})=o(\Psi_{\mathbb{SBM}(n;p^{2},Q^{2})}(H)).$

But, by Theorem 3.6, for any 2-SBM $\mathbb{SBM}(p,Q),$ it holds that

$$ \Psi_{\mathbb{SBM}(n;p,Q)}(H)\lesssim\max\Bigg(\Psi_{\mathbb{SBM}(n;p,Q)}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4}),\max_{1\leq t\leq 8}\Psi_{\mathbb{SBM}(n;p,Q)}(\mathsf{Star}_{t})\Bigg). $$

#### Proof.

Take $H=\mathsf{K}_{2,4}.$ Let $\mathbb{SBM}(n;p^{1},Q^{1})$ be just the SBM from Theorem A.2. Then, for any star $\mathsf{Star}_{t},$ $\displaystyle\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p^{1},Q^{1})}(\mathsf{Star}_{t})=0.$ However, as $\mathsf{K}_{2,4}$ has only even degree vertices, $\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p^{1},Q^{1})}(\mathsf{K}_{2,4})=1.$

Now, let $\mathbb{SBM}(n;p^{2},Q^{2})$ be the SBM with $p^{2}=(n^{-\alpha},1-n^{-\alpha})$ where $\alpha\in(0,1)$ and $Q^{2}=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\ 1&0\\ \end{pmatrix}.$ Then,

$$ \Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p^{2},Q^{2})}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4})\asymp\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(p^{2},Q^{2})}(\mathsf{K}_{4})\asymp(p^{2}_{1})^{2}=n^{-2\alpha}. $$

Thus,

$$ |\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(n;p^{2},Q^{2})}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4})|^{\frac{1}{|\mathsf{V}(\mathsf{Cyc}_{4})|}}\asymp n^{-\alpha/2}=o(|\Phi_{\mathbb{SBM}(n;p^{2},Q^{2})}(\mathsf{K}_{2,4})|^{\frac{1}{|\mathsf{V}(H))|}})=o(n^{-\alpha/3}).\qed $$

### B.1 Proof of Inequality (25)

We rewrite as follows.

#### Lemma B.1.

Suppose that $(p_{1},p_{2},\ldots,p_{k})$ is a pmf on $[k].$ Let $q_{1},q_{2},\ldots,q_{k}$ be real numbers in $[0,1].$ Then,

$$ v\longrightarrow\big(\sum_{i=1}^{k}p_{i}^{v}q_{i}^{v-1}\big)^{1/v} $$

is non-increasing on $[1,+\infty].$

#### Proof.

Define the function $\displaystyle f(v)\coloneqq\log\big(\sum_{i=1}^{k}p_{i}^{v}q_{i}^{v-1}\big)^{1/v}=\frac{1}{v}\log\big(\sum_{i=1}^{k}p_{i}^{v}q_{i}^{v-1}\big).$ It is enough to show that $f(v)$ is non-increasing. Equivalently, we need to show that $f^{\prime}(v)\leq 0.$

$$ \displaystyle f^{\prime}(v)\leq 0\Longleftrightarrow \displaystyle-\frac{1}{v^{2}}\log\big(\sum_{i=1}^{k}p_{i}^{v}q_{i}^{v-1}\big)+\frac{1}{v}\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{k}\log(p_{i}q_{i})p_{i}^{v}q_{i}^{v-1}}{\sum_{i=1}^{k}p_{i}^{v}q_{i}^{v-1}}\leq 0\Longleftrightarrow \displaystyle v\sum_{i=1}^{k}\log(p_{i}q_{i})p_{i}^{v}q_{i}^{v-1}\leq\log\big(\sum_{i=1}^{k}p_{i}^{v}q_{i}^{v-1}\big)\times\sum_{i=1}^{k}p_{i}^{v}q_{i}^{v-1}\Longleftrightarrow \displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{k}\log(p^{v}_{i}q^{v}_{i})p_{i}^{v}q_{i}^{v-1}\leq\sum_{i=1}^{k}\Bigg(\log\big(\sum_{i=1}^{k}p_{i}^{v}q_{i}^{v-1}\big)\times p_{i}^{v}q_{i}^{v-1}\Bigg). $$

The last inequality follows from the fact that $q_{i}\in[0,1]$ since for any $i,$

$$ \log(p^{v}_{i}q^{v}_{i})\leq\log(p^{v}_{i}q^{v-1}_{i})\leq\log\big(\sum_{i=1}^{k}p_{i}^{v}q_{i}^{v-1}\big).\qed $$
